The sibling rent-call surface (rentcalltotal.ejs:21) prints rent.total.grandTotal (7_total.ts:64-67, which INCLUDES vat) for the SAME data and is internally consistent. broken.trigger: Any tenant with occupant.vatRatio > 0 (VAT-liable / non-residential lease). Download or email the receipt ('ΑΠΟΔΕΙΞΗ ΕΙΣΠΡΑΞΗΣ', invoice document) for any term — GET /documents/invoice/:id/:term → data/invoice/index.js → utils.getRentsData(params,'invoice') (omitCharges=true at index.js:13).
broken.moneyImpact: Receipt to a VAT tenant prints a grand total understated by the full VAT amount (240 on a 1000/24% rent) and a 'balance remaining payable' that wrongly shows VAT still owed after full payment (or wrong credit on overpay). The legal Greek tax receipt does not foot — the sum of printed line-items does not equal the printed headline total — and reports money owed that was already paid.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED REAL in current code at f6f75966. I traced the full path independently. (1) preTaxAmount is the NET (pre-VAT) rent and 7_total.ts proves the businesslogic grandTotal adds +vat on top of it, so vat is a distinct, non-overlapping addend — not already folded into preTaxAmount. (2) For a VAT-liable tenant (occupant.vatRatio>0 → rentmanager.ts:791 → contract.vatRate), 4_vats.ts populates a non-empty rent.vats[] and 7_total.ts sets a non-zero rent.total.vat; both are persisted in occupant.rents[] (tenant.ts:142 Mixed) and flow unchanged through getRentsData's ...rent / ...rent.total spreads. (3) The receipt branch subTotal (index.js:122-127) and invoiceGrandTotal (132-133) never add vat; the rent-call branch falls back to canonical grandTotal which does. (4) The receipt body (invoicebody.ejs:47-91, header 'Total without VAT') renders only net line items, then invoicetotal.ejs prints a visible non-zero ΦΠΑ line (6-11), the previous balance (15-16), and the headline 'Σύνολο πληρωμής'=invoiceGrandTotal (20-21). So the printed footing (Total-before-VAT + ΦΠΑ + Previous balance) exceeds the printed 'Total with VAT' headline by exactly the VAT — the legal receipt does not foot. (5) newBalance=invoiceGrandTotal−payment: a tenant who pays the true amount owed (canonical grandTotal, e.g. 1240 on 1000/24%) gets newBalance=1000−1240=−240, wrongly printed as 'Πιστωτικό υπόλοιπο €240' (credit); a net-1000 payer shows 0 due despite owing VAT. Worked example matches: rent=1000, vatRatio=0.24 → rent.total.vat=240, canonical grandTotal=1240, but receipt headline=subTotal(1000)+balance(0)=1000, short by 240. This is NOT guarded, NOT a misread, and the rent-call half of the same fd6040bb change being correct is exactly what makes the receipt half a confirmed regression. Not round-1 territory (round 1 covered the tenant payment dialog and rent pipeline, not the PDF receipt VAT footing). Severity high: a Greek tax receipt that does not sum and reports VAT still owed after full payment.

verdict.reasoning:
Traced the full receipt path on disk at HEAD. For a VAT-liable tenant (contract.vatRate>0) whose rent also carries a property surcharge (rent.charges, e.g. property expenses pushed in 1_base.ts:890-911), the pipeline pushes a VAT line per charge (4_vats.ts:39-47) and folds it into rent.total.vat (7_total.ts:45-50). The receipt template suppresses the charge line-items (invoicebody.ejs:93-102) and the receipt data layer recomputes subTotal and invoiceGrandTotal to exclude those charges (data/index.js:122-141) — but it spreads ...rent.total and never overrides vat, so invoicetotal.ejs:10 prints the full pipeline VAT, which still contains the VAT computed on the omitted charge.

Worked example with rent=1000, charge=100, rate=0.24, no balance/payment: subTotal=1000, invoiceGrandTotal=1000, but printed VAT=rent.total.vat=264. The receipt shows Total-before-VAT=1000, VAT=264, Total-with-VAT=1000 — mutually inconsistent: 1000+264≠1000, and 264 is not 24% of the 1000 subtotal (correct VAT on shown lines = 240). The extra 24 is VAT on a 100 charge line that appears nowhere on the receipt. The leak is real and confined to the receipt path: charge-derived VAT lines remain in rent.total.vat after the data layer strips the charges from subTotal/grandTotal.

This is NOT round-1 territory (rent pipeline VAT math was about pipeline correctness; this is specifically the receipt's selective omission of charges from line-items+headline while leaving the VAT line whole). The minimal leak location: services/pdfgenerator/data/index.js IIFE at lines 135-141 — for omitCharges, it must also recompute vat to exclude the VAT lines whose source is rent.charges (or invoicetotal.ejs:10 must render a receipt-specific vat). Currently vat passes through via the ...rent.total spread.

Severity is medium-bounded: the receipt headline (invoiceGrandTotal=subTotal+balance) and Amount-paid/newBalance are computed independently of the VAT line, so the money the tenant is shown as paid and the balance remaining are NOT corrupted by this — only the displayed ΦΠΑ subtotal line is wrong/inflated, making the three printed rows (subTotal, VAT, total-with-VAT) internally inconsistent on a VAT tenant with charges. It is a wrong-rendered-value bug on an official tax-style document (ΑΠΟΔΕΙΞΗ ΕΙΣΠΡΑΞΗΣ), not a drop/double-count of received money.
verdict.correctedDetail: The reviewer's mechanism is correct and verified. Two refinements to the reviewer's framing: (1) The receipt headline is invoiceGrandTotal = subTotal + balance (data/index.js:133), computed independently of vat — so the headline does NOT silently absorb the charge-VAT; the inconsistency is that the printed VAT line (264) does not reconcile with the printed subTotal (1000) nor the printed total-with-VAT (1000). (2) The receipt does NOT use the pipeline grandTotal for the omitCharges branch (that is only used for rent-calls, line 132-134), so the 'headline being short by VAT (finding #1)' cross-reference is about rent-call/receipt headline composition; for the receipt the headline is self-consistent with subTotal but the standalone VAT row is the wrong figure. Net: VAT line is inflated by the VAT-on-omitted-charges (24 in the example: 264 shown vs 240 correct for displayed lines).

broken.brokenShape: propertyAddress is computed from dbTenant.properties[0] only ('First property only — multi-property tenants get the first one rendered'), while invoicebody.ejs:47-54 loops rent.preTaxAmounts (one per property; 1_base.ts builds one preTaxAmount per property) and prints a rent line for each. A 2-property tenant therefore gets a receipt listing rent for BOTH properties but a 'Διεύθυνση μισθίου' line naming only one.
broken.trigger: A single Occupant with two or more entries in properties[] (multi-unit lease). Download the receipt.
broken.moneyImpact: Rendering/labeling defect, not a money-math error — totals are correct. A multi-property receipt misstates which premises the charge is for, which weakens it as a tax document, but no money is dropped or double-counted.

verdict.codeEvidence: services/pdfgenerator/data/index.js:143-152 builds the customer-reference address line from the FIRST property only: ``` 143 // Property address line for the customer-reference table 144 // (Διεύθυνση μισθίου). First property only — multi-property 145 // tenants get the first one rendered; the table is a single row. 146 propertyAddress: (() => { 147 const addr = dbTenant.properties?.[0]?.propertyId?.address; 148 if (!addr) return ''; 149 return [addr.street1, addr.zipCode, addr.city] 150 .filter(Boolean) 151 .join(', '); 152 })() ``` That single string is rendered as one row in services/pdfgenerator/templates/partials/customerreference.ejs:11-15: ``` 11 <% if (rent.propertyAddress) { %> 12 13 <%=_.t('Property address')%> 14 <%= rent.propertyAddress %> ``` Meanwhile services/pdfgenerator/templates/partials/invoicebody.ejs:47-54 loops EVERY preTaxAmount, one rent line per entry: ``` 47 <% rent.preTaxAmounts.forEach(function(preTaxAmount) { %> 48 49 <%= rentLabel(preTaxAmount) %> ... 52 <%= _.formatNumber(preTaxAmount.amount, 'currency') %> ``` And the pipeline pushes ONE preTaxAmount per active property in services/api/src/businesslogic/tasks/1_base.ts:867-888: ``` 867 properties 868 .filter((property) => { ... currentMoment.isBetween(entryMoment, exitMoment ...) }) 879 .forEach(function (property) { 880 if (property.property) { 881 const name = property.property.name || ''; 882 const preTaxAmount = Math.round((Number(property.rent) || 0) * 100) / 100; 885 rent.preTaxAmounts.push({ description: name, amount: preTaxAmount }); ``` Both partials receive the same `rent` object in invoice.ejs:18,22 (receipt) and rentcall.ejs:12,29 (rent call).
verdict.reasoning: The claim holds in current code. I independently traced the full path. (1) 1_base.ts:867-888 iterates contract.properties filtered ONLY by entry/exit-date overlap with the term and pushes one preTaxAmount per active property — so a single Occupant with two concurrently-active properties yields preTaxAmounts.length === 2. (2) invoicebody.ejs:47-54 renders one rent line for each preTaxAmount, so the document body shows both properties' rent. (3) data/index.js:146-152 computes propertyAddress strictly from dbTenant.properties[0] (explicit code comment: "First property only — multi-property tenants get the first one rendered"). (4) customerreference.ejs:11-15 renders that single string as one 'Property address' row. (5) Both partials are included with the same `rent` object in invoice.ejs (receipt, line 18/22) and rentcall.ejs (line 12/29), so the defect ships on both receipts and rent-calls. The trigger — a single Occupant with >=2 properties active in the same term — is a real supported data shape (multi-unit lease, called out in the project domain facts). This is a rendering/labeling defect, NOT a money-math error: total (data/index.js:108-142) sums buildingCharges/preTaxAmount/charges via rent.total fields and is fully independent of propertyAddress, so no money is dropped or double-counted. The receipt is weakened as a tax document because the 'Διεύθυνση μισθίου' line names only one premises while the body charges rent for both. Matches the reviewer's stated severity (low). Minimal leak location: the propertyAddress IIFE at data/index.js:146-152 hard-indexes [0] instead of joining all active properties' addresses (or the customerreference.ejs row should iterate). Note the date-overlap filter in 1_base means the body actually renders only properties active in the term, so the address line should likewise reflect the active set, not literally properties[0].

verdict.reasoning:
Worked example (rent 1000, vatRatio 0.24, no charges/balance/debts/discount), traced through code I read:
- Pipeline: preTaxAmount=1000; 4_vats pushes vat amount=round(1000*0.24*100)/100=240 → rent.vats=[{rate:0.24,amount:240}], rent.total.vat=240; 7_total grandTotal=1000+240=1240.
- Receipt path in data/index.js (omitCharges=true): subTotal=1000+0+0-0+0=1000 (no vat); invoiceGrandTotal=round((1000+0)*100)/100=1000 (no vat); newBalance=1000-0=1000.
- invoicetotal.ejs renders: Σύνολο πριν ΦΠΑ=1000, ΦΠΑ 24%=240, Προηγούμενο υπόλοιπο=0, Σύνολο πληρωμής=1000.
Printed lines sum to 1000+240=1240 but the "Total with VAT"/Σύνολο πληρωμής headline shows 1000 — internally inconsistent by exactly rent.total.vat (240). If the tenant pays the real 1240, newBalance=1000-1240=-240 → invoicetotal.ejs:32 shows "Credit balance €240" (phantom credit). If they pay 1000, newBalance=0 → shows fully paid while €240 VAT remains owed.

Refutation attempts all failed: (1) invoice/index.js post-processing only sets documentDate/cssUrl/logoUrl — does not zero vat; (2) no guard strips rent.vats or rent.total.vat on the receipt path; (3) the rent-call path correctly uses grandTotal (which includes vat), so only the receipt branch is wrong — exactly as the reviewer scoped it. The omitCharges flag legitimately excludes property charges from the body, but it ALSO inadvertently excludes VAT from the headline math while the VAT line is still printed.

Note: the reviewer cited invoicetotal.ejs grand-total at ":20-21" and rentcalltotal at ":21". On disk invoicetotal.ejs:20-21 is indeed the "Total with VAT" row (prints rent.total.invoiceGrandTotal) and rentcalltotal.ejs:21 prints rent.total.grandTotal — both line citations match the file. The data/index.js line citations (122-127 subTotal, 132-134 invoiceGrandTotal, 140 newBalance) also match disk exactly.

verdict.codeEvidence: services/emailer/src/emailparts/contents/rentcall/body_html.ejs:32 (the summary/total row of the breakdown table): `<%- _.t('Total') %><%- _.formatNumber(rent.total.grandTotal, 'currency') %>` Table guard at body_html.ejs:21 renders the table when buildingCharges/multiple preTaxAmounts/charges exist: `<% if ((rent.buildingCharges && rent.buildingCharges.length) || (rent.preTaxAmounts && rent.preTaxAmounts.length > 1) || (rent.charges && rent.charges.length)) { %>` services/emailer/src/utils/templatefunctions.ts:9-10 — `_.t` is a raw passthrough to i18n.__: ` t: (...params: any[]) => {` ` return (i18n.__ as any)(...params);` services/emailer/src/emailcontent.ts:41 — the `_` helper (bound to realm `locale`) is injected into the EJS data: ` _: templateFunctions({ locale, currency })` and emailcontent.ts:47-50 renders body_html.ejs with that data. services/emailer/src/index.ts:22-26 — i18n configured with updateFiles:false and the 6 locales; This is a real i18n leak on a money-bearing tenant email, matching the reviewer's claim including the mechanism and exact line. broken.brokenShape: _incomingTenants's returned JSON object (accountingmanager.ts:199-208) intentionally has NO endDate key (Wave-24 B15 dropped it as 'misleading'). The Incoming tab UI still reads tenant.endDate at IncomingTenants.js:38 and renders moment(tenant.endDate).format('L'). Since tenant.endDate is undefined in the response, moment(undefined) returns the CURRENT moment, so format('L') prints today's date. Verified: moment(undefined).format('L') -> '06/16/2026'.
broken.trigger: Open Accounting > Incoming tenants tab for a year with any incoming tenant. Every row's date range reads '<beginDate> - <today>'. The displayed contract end changes every day the page is viewed and is never the tenant's real contract end.
broken.moneyImpact: No money mis-computation, but every incoming tenant's contract period is rendered with a fabricated end date equal to the viewing day — a wrong, non-deterministic value the landlord may copy into records or trust as the lease end.

verdict.codeEvidence:
accountingmanager.ts:199-207 (`all()` calls `_incomingTenants(tenants)` with rawData defaulting true) returns ONLY these keys — no endDate: ``` return { _id: tenant._id, name: tenant.name, reference: tenant.reference, properties: _properties(tenant, rawData), beginDate, terminationDate, guaranty: NumberFormat.format(_round(tenant.guaranty || 0)) }; ``` The Wave-24 B15 comment (lines 186-192) confirms endDate was deliberately dropped from the incoming JSON/CSV. IncomingTenants.js:36-39 still reads tenant.endDate: ```
{moment(tenant.beginDate).format('L')} -{' '} {moment(tenant.endDate).format('L')}
``` Data path carries no endDate: restcalls.js:50-51 `const response = await apiFetcher().get('/accounting/${year}'); return response.data;` (verbatim). accounting/[year].js:88-96 sets `filteredData.incomingTenants` = `accountingData.incomingTenants` (no search) or a name-only `.filter()` of it (search) — neither adds endDate. moment(undefined) behavior (executed in repo node/moment): `moment(undefined).format('L')` => `06/16/2026`, isValid: true. (moment(null) is Invalid, but the field is undefined, not null.)
verdict.reasoning: The claim HOLDS as a real current-code bug. I traced the full path: (1) the JSON API path (rawData=true, used by `all()` at line 408) returns incoming-tenant objects that intentionally omit `endDate` per Wave-24 B15 (lines 186-192, return object lines 199-207); (2) `fetchAccounting` returns the response verbatim; (3) the page either passes the API array straight through or applies a name-only filter — no transform re-adds `endDate`; (4) `IncomingTenants.js:38` still renders `moment(tenant.endDate).format('L')` with `tenant.endDate === undefined`; (5) I confirmed in node that `moment(undefined)` is a VALID moment equal to now, so `.format('L')` prints the viewing day (06/16/2026), not a blank or "Invalid date". The B15 change removed the field from the API but left the matching consumer line in the component, so every incoming-tenant row in the UI shows `<beginDate> - <today>`, a fabricated, non-deterministic contract end. No money mis-computation, but a wrong/non-deterministic value rendered to the landlord — matches the spec's "render a wrong value" criterion (sev medium). Note: the CSV export path is NOT affected (its field list at lines 426-433 correctly has no endDate column); the leak is confined to the UI component. Minimal fix: drop or guard the ` - {moment(tenant.endDate).format('L')}` segment at IncomingTenants.js:37-38.

broken.title: Settlements CSV fabricates a contract-end date (export day) for any tenant lacking both terminationDate and endDate; on-screen JSON shows blank/Invalid — CSV and UI disagree
broken.line: accountingmanager.ts:295-299 (`endDate = rawData ? terminationDate||endDate : moment.utc(terminationDate||endDate).format('YYYY-MM-DD')`); tenant.ts:56-58 (beginDate/endDate/terminationDate all optional)
broken.brokenShape: In the non-rawData (CSV/print) branch, endDate = moment.utc(tenant.terminationDate || tenant.endDate).format('YYYY-MM-DD'). When a tenant has neither field (schema allows it: tenant.ts:56-58 are plain Date, no required; a mongo-backdoor/legacy import row with rents but no end/termination is valid), moment.utc(undefined) returns NOW, so the multiline 'tenant' cell (settlements 'tenant' string at :388-392 embeds `${beginDate} - ${endDate}`) prints '... - 2026-06-16' (the export day). The rawData JSON path (:296) returns undefined, so the on-screen TenantSettlements header (TenantSettlements.js:229-230 moment(settlement.endDate).format('L')) renders today too — but the two surfaces derive it independently and the value is a meaningless fabricated date in both.
broken.trigger: Seed (via mongo direct insert) a tenant with rents[].year=2026 and no endDate/terminationDate, then download /csv/settlements/2026. The Tenant column's contract period reads '<begin> - <today>'. Re-export tomorrow and the same tenant's end date shifts by one day.
broken.moneyImpact: No money figure is wrong, but the exported accounting CSV carries a fabricated contract-end equal to the export day for affected tenants — corrupts any downstream reconciliation that keys on contract period and silently changes between exports.

```
accountingmanager.ts:388-392 (fabricated date embedded in the multiline 'tenant' CSV cell):
```
            : `${tenant.name}\n${
                tenant.reference
              }\n${beginDate} - ${endDate}\n${i18n.__('Deposit: {{deposit}}', {
```
accountingmanager.ts:479 (CSV path passes rawData=false): `const data = _settlements(tenants, realm.locale, realm.currency, false);`
accountingmanager.ts:46-49 (_fetchData $match — selects ANY tenant with rents.year=year; no end/termination filter): `$match: { realmId, 'rents.year': year }`
tenant.ts:56-58 (all three date fields optional, plain Date): `beginDate: Date,` / `endDate: Date,` / `terminationDate: Date,`
Empirical: `moment.utc(undefined).format('YYYY-MM-DD')` -> `2026-06-16` and `isValid()===true` (run on disk's moment).
Contrast — sibling functions DO guard the same hazard: _incomingTenants accountingmanager.ts:193-197 and _outgoingTenants 236-240 both use `tenant.terminationDate ? moment.utc(...).format(...) : ''`; _settlements omits that guard.
Frontend UI (rawData=true path, endDate=undefined): TenantSettlements.js:229-230 `{moment(settlement.beginDate).format('L')} - {moment(settlement.endDate).format('L')}` — and `moment(undefined).format('L')` returns today (`06/16/2026`), valid.
verdict.reasoning: The core defect is real in CURRENT code and unguarded. Traced path: GET settlements CSV -> settlementsAsCsv (line 470) -> _settlements(..., false). _fetchData's $match (lines 46-49) pulls EVERY tenant with a rent in the target year, with no requirement that endDate or terminationDate be set; the schema (tenant.ts:56-58) makes both optional plain Dates, so a mongo-backdoor/legacy row with rents but neither field is valid (and the project's own audit rules explicitly treat mongo-direct-insert legacy rows as in-scope). In the non-rawData branch (lines 295-299) endDate = moment.utc(tenant.terminationDate || tenant.endDate).format('YYYY-MM-DD'); when both are falsy this is moment.utc(undefined), which I confirmed empirically is VALID and returns NOW (2026-06-16). That fabricated date is interpolated into the multiline 'tenant' cell at lines 388-392 as `${beginDate} - ${endDate}`, so the settlements CSV's contract period reads '<begin> - <export-day>' and shifts by a day on each re-export. The intended pattern exists right next to it: _incomingTenants (193-197) and _outgoingTenants (236-240) both guard terminationDate with `? moment.utc(...) : ''`; _settlements simply omits the guard. No money figure is wrong (sev low), but the export carries a fabricated, drifting contract-end that corrupts downstream period-keyed reconciliation. I am marking BROKEN (i.e. the reviewer's finding stands) with one correction: the reviewer's secondary claim that 'on-screen JSON shows blank/Invalid' and that 'CSV and UI disagree' is inaccurate — in rawData=true endDate is undefined, and the UI's local moment(undefined).format('L') (TenantSettlements.js:229-230) is ALSO valid and renders today, so CSV and UI actually AGREE on a fabricated export-day, not disagree. The defect (fabricated/drifting contract-end on tenants lacking both dates) is the real issue; minimal fix is to add the same `? ... : ''` falsy-guard to the endDate expression at accountingmanager.ts:295-299 that the sibling functions already use.
verdict.correctedDetail: Finding HOLDS as a real low-sev bug, with one factual correction. The leak is the missing falsy-guard at accountingmanager.ts:295-299: `moment.utc(tenant.terminationDate || tenant.endDate)` becomes `moment.utc(undefined)` (= today, valid) when a tenant with rents in the year has neither field — a schema-valid state (tenant.ts:56-58, both optional). The fabricated date lands in the settlements CSV 'tenant' cell at lines 388-392. CORRECTION to the reviewer: the on-screen UI does NOT show blank/Invalid and does NOT disagree with the CSV — TenantSettlements.js:229-230 uses local moment(undefined).format('L') which is valid and also renders today (06/16/2026). Both surfaces fabricate the same export-day; they agree on a wrong value rather than disagreeing. Minimal fix: guard endDate identically to _incomingTenants (193-197) / _outgoingTenants (236-240): `tenant.terminationDate || tenant.endDate ? moment.utc(...).format('YYYY-MM-DD') : ''`.

broken.title: /accounting/:year and all three CSV exports 500 for a tenant with a year-matching rent but null/missing properties array (_properties calls .map on null)
broken.line: accountingmanager.ts:151-161 (_properties does tenant.properties.map without a `|| []` guard); :43-64 aggregation $map over missing $properties yields null; called from :153/:160/:203/:264/:392
broken.brokenShape: The aggregation projects properties via $map over $properties (:54-64). In MongoDB, $map over a missing/null input field yields null. _properties (:151) then does `tenant.properties.map(...)` with no defensive `(properties || [])`. A tenant document that matches 'rents.year': year but whose properties field is null/absent (corrupt or backdoor-seeded legacy row) makes _properties throw TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'map') — verified — taking down the entire /accounting/:year response AND incoming/outgoing/settlements CSV exports for the whole realm, not just that one tenant.
broken.trigger: Mongo-insert (Occupant) a row with rents:[{year:<Y>,...}] and properties unset/null, then GET /accounting/<Y> or any /csv/* for that year. The endpoint 500s for every tenant in the realm because the map crashes mid-aggregation-consumption.
broken.moneyImpact: One malformed legacy/imported tenant row makes the entire year's accounting page and all CSV exports unavailable (hard 500) for that realm until the row is repaired — a denial of the accounting surface rather than a money mis-count.

verdict.reasoning:
I independently traced the exact path on disk. The claim holds in CURRENT code:

- The $match (lines 46-49) gates only on realmId + rents.year, so a tenant whose `properties` is null/absent but has a year-matching rent passes through.
- $map over a missing/null input field yields null in MongoDB (well-documented aggregation behavior), and there is no $ifNull coalesce in the pipeline, so the projected `properties` is null.
- `.aggregate()` returns raw POJOs, so Mongoose's array default ([]) never repairs the value.
- _properties (151-161) and the settlements branch (392) call `.map()` on that null with no `|| []` / `?.` guard, throwing TypeError, which asyncWrapper converts to a 500 for the whole-realm response (the .map runs while iterating the tenant array, so one bad row fails the entire year/CSV, not just that tenant).

The settlements-CSV path (line 392) is the strongest: it fires for ANY matched tenant regardless of incoming/outgoing flags, whereas 153/160 require the malformed tenant to also be incoming/outgoing. Either way the surface goes down.

Severity is genuinely low: this is an availability/DoS of the accounting + CSV surfaces triggered by a corrupt/backdoor-seeded legacy row, not a money mis-count, and the trigger requires a malformed document (the API's own validators would normally prevent persisting properties: null). But the steering docs explicitly note that legacy/imported/mongo-seeded rows with such drift exist and are a real scenario in this codebase, and the conspicuous absence of the guard that every sibling manager applies makes this a concrete, reproducible defect rather than a theoretical one. The reviewer's file:line citations all match disk.
verdict.correctedDetail: Reviewer's analysis is accurate. One refinement on the "all three CSV exports + /accounting/:year" scope: the unconditional crash is the settlements path (line 392 for CSV, and line 315 `tenant.rents.forEach` is safe because rents IS projected as an array). The _properties crashes at 153 (rawData JSON via /accounting/:year) and 160 (incoming/outgoing CSV) require the malformed tenant to additionally satisfy the incoming or outgoing predicate (beginDate-in-year, or terminationDate-in-year) before _properties is invoked on it; if the corrupt row is neither incoming nor outgoing, the JSON /accounting/:year and the two incoming/outgoing CSVs survive but the settlements CSV (line 392, no such filter) still 500s. So "settlements CSV 500s for any year-matching malformed row" is guaranteed; the other three 500 conditionally on the row being flagged incoming/outgoing. Minimal fix: coalesce in the helper, e.g. `(tenant.properties || []).map(...)` at 153/160/392, or add `properties: { $ifNull: [ { $map: {...} }, [] ] }` in the $addFields at line 54.

broken.title: Incoming-tenants tab renders TODAY's date as every tenant's contract end (server dropped endDate, client still reads it)
broken.line: 37-38 (client) reads tenant.endDate; services/api/src/managers/accountingmanager.ts:199-208 (server _incomingTenants return object) omits endDate
broken.brokenShape: _incomingTenants returns { _id, name, reference, properties, beginDate, terminationDate, guaranty } — NO endDate field (intentionally dropped per the Wave-24 B15 comment at accountingmanager.ts:186-192). But IncomingTenants.js:37-38 still renders `{moment(tenant.beginDate).format('L')} - {moment(tenant.endDate).format('L')}`. tenant.endDate is undefined, and moment(undefined) returns the current moment (verified: moment(undefined).format('L') -> 06/16/2026, isValid()===true). So the right side of the date range is silently set to TODAY.
broken.trigger: Open Accounting -> Incoming tenants for any realm. Every incoming tenant's date range renders as `<beginDate> - <today>`, e.g. '01/03/2024 - 16/06/2026'. The displayed end date changes every single day and is never the tenant's actual contract end. The CSV export (which correctly omits the column) and the on-screen view now disagree, and the on-screen view shows a fabricated date.
broken.moneyImpact: No money is mis-summed, but the landlord reads a wrong-and-plausible contract end date for every incoming tenant — a date that silently advances daily. They cannot tell which tenants' leases actually expire when from this tab.

verdict.codeEvidence:
CLIENT — webapps/landlord/src/components/accounting/IncomingTenants.js lines 36-39: 36
37 {moment(tenant.beginDate).format('L')} -{' '} 38 {moment(tenant.endDate).format('L')} 39
The component renders tenant.endDate directly with no fallback/guard. SERVER — services/api/src/managers/accountingmanager.ts, _incomingTenants return object (rawData defaults true), lines 199-208: 199 return { 200 _id: tenant._id, 201 name: tenant.name, 202 reference: tenant.reference, 203 properties: _properties(tenant, rawData), 204 beginDate, 205 terminationDate, 206 guaranty: NumberFormat.format(_round(tenant.guaranty || 0)) 207 }; No endDate key. The drop is intentional per the Wave-24 B15 comment, lines 186-192: 186 // Wave-24 B15: tenant.endDate reflects the post-renewal end (incoming ... 190 // misleading endDate from the incoming CSV/JSON entirely. JSON route that feeds the on-screen tab (line 408): `incomingTenants: _incomingTenants(tenants)` — rawData=true, same object shape, no endDate. DATA FLOW — webapps/landlord/src/pages/[organization]/accounting/[year].js: line 63: useQuery fetches accountingData (the /all JSON above) lines 93-96: filteredData.incomingTenants is a name-substring `.filter(...)` passthrough of accountingData.incomingTenants — never adds endDate lines 219-221: So the component receives objects with no endDate property. RUNTIME CONFIRMATION — node -e on the repo's moment 2.29.4: moment(undefined).isValid() === true moment(undefined).format('L') === '06/16/2026' (today) The CSV export correctly omits the column (fields list lines 426-433 has no endDate); only the on-screen view fabricates it.
verdict.reasoning: I independently traced the full path on disk at HEAD f6f75966. The server function _incomingTenants returns an object literal (lines 199-208) that deliberately omits endDate — confirmed by the Wave-24 B15 comment (lines 186-192) and the matching CSV fields list (lines 426-433) which also drops the "Contract end date" column. The on-screen JSON route (line 408) calls _incomingTenants(tenants) with rawData defaulting to true, producing the exact same endDate-less object shape. The landlord page fetches this via useQuery (line 63) and passes it to <IncomingTenants> through filteredData (lines 93-96, 219-221), which is a pure name-substring filter that preserves each server object verbatim and never re-injects endDate. The component then renders moment(tenant.endDate).format('L') at line 38 with no guard. Because tenant.endDate is undefined, moment(undefined) yields the current moment — I confirmed against the repo's installed moment 2.29.4 that moment(undefined).isValid() is true and .format('L') returns today's date (06/16/2026). Therefore every incoming tenant's date range renders as "<beginDate> - <today>", a plausible-but-fabricated contract end that advances every day. No money is mis-summed, but a wrong, daily-advancing date is shown for every incoming tenant, and the on-screen view disagrees with the (correct) CSV export. Minimal leak location: IncomingTenants.js line 38 reading a field the server no longer supplies — the fix is to either stop rendering the end-date side (matching the CSV) or guard moment(tenant.endDate) with a validity/presence check (e.g. only render when tenant.endDate is truthy).

broken.title: Legacy/typeless payment (type:'' with amount>0) crashes the entire Payments settlements tab
broken.line: 167 (t(type[0].toUpperCase() + type.slice(1))); reachable because accountingmanager.ts:317-326 passes payment.type through raw and rentmanager.ts:1108 persists type: payment.type || ''
broken.brokenShape: SettlementList renders, for every payment with amount>0, `t(type[0].toUpperCase() + type.slice(1))`. When type is '' (empty string) type[0] is undefined, so undefined.toUpperCase() throws TypeError; when type is missing entirely the same throw occurs. The throw is inside data.map(), so it takes down the WHOLE Payments tab render, not just one row. The server-side guard at rentmanager.ts:820-830 only rejects a NEW empty-string type when p.type is explicitly sent (`if (p?.type !== undefined && p.type !== null)`), and only for amount>0; it does not migrate pre-Wave-26 rows, and a payment that omits type entirely (undefined) skips the guard and is stored as type:'' at rentmanager.ts:1108.
broken.trigger: A realm with any legacy payment row where amount>0 and type==='' (the guard comment at rentmanager.ts:816-819 explicitly states 'Older legacy callers tolerated empty strings'), OR any future write that omits the type field. On this production NAS (months of pre-Wave-26 data) such a row makes the Payments tab throw on render the moment that tenant is in the year's settlements.
broken.moneyImpact: The entire Payments (settlements) accounting tab for the year is blanked by a render crash whenever one tenant has a typeless recorded payment — the landlord loses the per-month payment grid for ALL tenants in that year, not just the offending one.

verdict.codeEvidence:
webapps/landlord/src/components/accounting/TenantSettlements.js:155-168 (the crash site): 155 {hasSettlements 156 ? settlements.map((settlement, index) => { 157 const { date, amount, type } = settlement; 158 return amount > 0 ? ( ... 166
167 {t(type[0].toUpperCase() + type.slice(1))} 168
JS semantics verified via node: type==='' -> ''[0] is undefined -> undefined.toUpperCase() => TypeError "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toUpperCase')" type===undefined -> undefined[0] => TypeError "...(reading '0')" The only guard before this line is `amount > 0` (line 158) — type is NOT checked. Read side passes type through raw (services/api/src/managers/accountingmanager.ts): 43 async function _fetchData(realmId, year) { return await Collections.Tenant.aggregate([ ... 72 payments: '$$rent.payments', // raw projection, no normalization 317 settlements[month - 1] = payments.map( 318 ({ date, type, amount, reference }) => ({ 322 date: moment.utc(date,'DD/MM/YYYY',true).toDate(), 323 type, // <- straight from stored doc 324 amount, reference })); 410 settlements: _settlements(tenants, realm.locale, realm.currency) // rawData defaults true No schema enforcement (services/common/src/collections/tenant.ts): 142 rents: [mongoose.Schema.Types.Mixed], // free-form; payment.type can be '' or absent Write side lets type='' / omitted-type persist (services/api/src/managers/rentmanager.ts): 816 // Older legacy callers tolerated empty strings; ... 820 if (p?.type !== undefined && p.type !== null) { // omitted type (undefined) skips the whole block 821 if (p.type === '' && Number(p?.amount) > 0) { throw new ServiceError(...,422); } 827 if (p.type !== '') { validateEnum(p.type, PAYMENT_TYPES, ...); } 828 } 1108 type: payment.type || '', // undefined/'' both persisted as '' Recompute (line 1052-1056) rebuilds payments ONLY for the single _targetTermNum, so legacy ''-type rows in untouched terms never get migrated. Error boundary scope (webapps/landlord/src/pages/_app.js): 117 121 125 ErrorBoundary.js:66 getDerivedStateFromError -> render ErrorFallback for the whole page.
verdict.reasoning: The bug is real in current code. I traced the full path end-to-end: (1) tenant.ts:142 stores rents as Schema.Types.Mixed with zero enforcement on payment.type; (2) rentmanager.ts:820 only validates type when it is explicitly present (`p.type !== undefined && p.type !== null`), so a payment that OMITS type with amount>0 bypasses the guard, and rentmanager.ts:1108 then writes `type: payment.type || ''` = '' — plus the code's own comment at 816-819 acknowledges legacy rows already carry empty strings and are never migrated (recompute at 1052 only rebuilds the single target term's payments); (3) accountingmanager.ts _fetchData (line 43) is a raw mongo aggregate projecting payments straight from storage (line 72) and _settlements line 322-323 passes type through untouched to the UI (rawData defaults true, called from all() at line 410); (4) TenantSettlements.js:167 does `t(type[0].toUpperCase() + type.slice(1))` for every payment with amount>0 — I confirmed via node that type==='' and type===undefined both throw TypeError. The throw occurs inside data.map()/SettlementList render under the single app-root ErrorBoundary (_app.js:117), so it replaces the ENTIRE accounting page with the error fallback. The reviewer's mechanism, trigger (legacy/omitted-type payment with amount>0), and high severity are all correct; the only nuance is the blast radius is the whole accounting page via ErrorBoundary, even broader than the claimed 'Payments tab blanks'. Minimal fix is at TenantSettlements.js:167, e.g. guard with `type ? t(type[0].toUpperCase() + type.slice(1)) : ''`.

broken.title: CSV formula-injection guard (_sanitizeCsvText) is applied to ZERO fields that actually reach a CSV file
broken.line: 31-41 (guard); applied only at 351-355 (rawData JSON notes); CSV export fields name/reference/properties emitted raw at 201-203, 262-264, 388-392
broken.brokenShape: _sanitizeCsvText's docstring (lines 19-30) claims to neutralise formula injection in 'any free-text field that ends up in the export'. In practice it is called ONLY inside the rawData===true branch (notesByMonth, lines 351-355), which feeds the on-screen React UI — NOT a CSV. The three real CSV exporters (incomingTenantsAsCsv, outgoingTenantsAsCsv, settlementsAsCsv, rawData===false) emit tenant.name (201/262), tenant.reference (202/263), property names (_properties join at 160), and the multiline settlements 'tenant' string (388-392) completely unsanitised. tenant.name/reference have no character validation (validators.ts validateStringField only checks length/whitespace), so '=HYPERLINK(...)' or '=cmd|...' is stored verbatim.
broken.trigger: Create/import a tenant named e.g. '=HYPERLINK("http://evil","x")' or with reference '=cmd|'/C calc'!A1' (passes all server validation). Landlord clicks the CSV download icon on Incoming/Outgoing/Payments and opens the file in Excel/LibreOffice/Sheets -> the cell is evaluated as a formula. The very guard added to stop this protects only the JSON path no spreadsheet ever sees.
broken.moneyImpact: No money mis-count, but the accountant's machine executes attacker/tenant-controlled spreadsheet formulas on CSV open — the exact RCE/exfil vector the guard was written to close, left fully open on the export path.

verdict.codeEvidence:
accountingmanager.ts: the guard `_sanitizeCsvText` (lines 31-41) is called ONLY at lines 352-354, and `grep -n "_sanitizeCsvText"` confirms no other call sites. Those three calls sit strictly inside `if (rawData) {` (the branch opens at line 316: `tenant.rents.forEach(({ month, payments, description, discounts, debts }) => { if (rawData) {`), i.e. the rawData JSON path that feeds the React UI — not a CSV. Lines 351-355: `notesByMonth[month - 1] = { description: _sanitizeCsvText(desc), notepromo: _sanitizeCsvText(np), noteextracharge: _sanitizeCsvText(ne) };`.

The three real CSV exporters all call their builders with rawData=false: `incomingTenantsAsCsv` line 423 `_incomingTenants(tenants, realm.locale, realm.currency, false)`; `outgoingTenantsAsCsv` line 450 `_outgoingTenants(..., false)`; `settlementsAsCsv` line 479 `_settlements(..., false)`. Each then runs `new Parser({fields,...}).parse(data)` (434-435, 464-465, 486-487) and `res.send(csv)` with `Content-Type: text/csv`.

The builders emit attacker-controllable free text completely unsanitized:
- `_incomingTenants` lines 200-203: `name: tenant.name, reference: tenant.reference, properties: _properties(tenant, rawData)`.
- `_outgoingTenants` lines 261-264: same `name`/`reference`/`properties`.
- `_settlements` rawData=false branch lines 387-392: `tenant: ... ${tenant.name}\n${tenant.reference}\n... ${tenant.properties.map(({name})=>name).join('\n')}`; payment cell strings at 358-369 also embed raw `reference`.
- `_properties` line 160 (rawData=false): `tenant.properties.map(({name})=>name).join('\n')` — raw names.

The docstring at 19-30 explicitly claims the guard neutralises "any free-text field that ends up in the export" and that a tenant note "would execute on the accountant's machine," yet the only protected path is the JSON branch a spreadsheet never sees.

validators.ts: `validateStringLength` (186-219) and `validateStringField` (226-258) check ONLY type, trim/whitespace, and min/max length — no rejection of leading `= + - @`. occupantmanager.ts validates `name` via `validateStringField` (lines 930, 1194; only trim+length) and takes `reference` as-is (line 60 `reference: tenant.reference || nanoid()`). So a tenant named `=HYPERLINK("http://evil","x")` or with reference `=cmd|'/C calc'!A1` passes all server validation and is persisted verbatim, then emitted raw into every CSV.

routes.ts 465-474 wires the three live CSV endpoints (`/csv/tenants/incoming/:year`, `/csv/tenants/outgoing/:year`, `/csv/settlements/:year`) to these exporters.
verdict.reasoning: Independently traced and confirmed. The `_sanitizeCsvText` formula-injection guard is invoked at exactly one place (lines 352-354), which is gated by `if (rawData)` (line 316). All three CSV-producing routes invoke their builders with rawData=false, so that branch never runs for any CSV. On the CSV path, tenant.name, tenant.reference, and joined property names are passed to json2csv completely unsanitized (incoming 201-203, outgoing 262-264, settlements 388-392, _properties join 160). verdict.codeEvidence:
webapps/landlord/src/components/accounting/TenantSettlements.js:13 `const months = moment.localeData().months();` (module-level, no locale arg). Consumed at :122 `const monthName = months[month][0].toUpperCase() + months[month].slice(1);` and rendered at :141 `{monthName}`, and iterated at :233 `{months.map((_m, index) => {`.

moment.js:2182-2185 — defineLocale has a "backwards compat" side effect: `getSetGlobalLocale(name)`, so each `import 'moment/locale/<x>'` sets the global locale to the locale being defined; the LAST import (es) wins.
moment.js:2080 `return globalLocale;` — `moment.localeData()` with no arg returns the active global locale object.
moment.js:967-972 `localeMonths` returns `this._months` (the literal array snapshot) when called with no moment arg.

Server CSV path is correctly realm-pinned: services/api/src/managers/accountingmanager.ts:480 `const months = moment.localeData(realm.locale).months();` (explicit realm.locale arg), used at :483 as the CSV column headers.

NumberFormat resolves locale LIVE from the store, not the frozen const: hooks/useFormatNumber.js:13-16 use `store.organization.selected.locale`.

Empirical reproduction with _app.js's exact import order (fr,pt,de,el,es) under node@20: global locale after imports = `es`; frozen `months` = `['enero','febrero','marzo',...]`; after `moment.locale('el')` the frozen const STAYS `['enero','febrero','marzo']`; server path `moment.localeData('el').months()` = `['Ιανουάριος','Φεβρουάριος',...]`. verdict.reasoning:
The core mechanism is real in CURRENT code. `months` (line 13) is captured once at module-import time from `moment.localeData()` (no arg → globalLocale), and is a fixed array snapshot — `localeMonths` (moment.js:967-972) returns the literal `_months` array. Later `moment.locale(realm)` calls in MyApp (_app.js:64) reassign globalLocale but do NOT mutate the already-captured const. I empirically confirmed under node@20 that with _app.js's exact locale-import order the frozen array is Spanish and stays Spanish after `moment.locale('el')`, while the server CSV path (accountingmanager.ts:480) explicitly passes `realm.locale` and yields Greek. So on a Greek realm, when TenantSettlements.js's module body executes before MyApp's first render sets the realm locale (the case on a direct page load / hard refresh of the accounting page, where the page chunk's module body runs during webpack instantiation before React's first render), the month-row labels (lines 122/141) and the month-column ordering render in the non-realm locale, diverging from the locale-pinned CSV export and from NumberFormat (which reads store.organization.selected.locale live). This is a genuine wrong-locale render, matching the reviewer's low severity (no money error).

Two corrections to the reviewer's claim, neither of which negates the finding: (1) The frozen locale is 'es' (Spanish), not 'en' as stated — because `defineLocale`'s backwards-compat side effect (moment.js:2185) makes the LAST locale import ('moment/locale/es', _app.js:6) the active global, not the moment built-in 'en' default. The mismatch direction is identical; only the wrong language differs. (2) The date `moment(date).format('L')` portion (lines 164/229-230) is largely NOT broken: those moments are constructed during React render, after MyApp:64 has already run `moment.locale(realm)`, so they pick up the realm locale live and format correctly. The genuinely-frozen-and-divergent part is specifically the `months` const (line 13 → 122/141), the month-name row labels. The minimal leak is line 13; the fix is to derive `months` from the realm locale at render time (e.g. `moment.localeData(store.organization.selected.locale).months()` inside the component) instead of freezing at module load.

broken.brokenShape: The 'a non-zero payment must have a type' check is nested inside `if (p?.type !== undefined && p.type !== null)`. When a payment is submitted with amount>0 and type omitted or explicitly null, that outer condition is false, so the required-type check at 821 is skipped entirely; the payment is then stored as type: payment.type || '' === '' with a positive amount. On the Accounting page, _settlements rawData passes type straight through (line 318); TenantSettlements.js renders the payment because amount>0 (line 158) and executes t(type[0].toUpperCase() + type.slice(1)) — but type==='' makes type[0] undefined, so undefined.toUpperCase() throws TypeError and the Payments tab render crashes (error boundary / blank tab).
broken.trigger: POST/PATCH a rent payment with {amount: 100} and no type field (or type:null) — a crafted request or a pre-guard legacy row. Then open Accounting → Payments for that year; the tab throws on the affected tenant's month.
broken.moneyImpact: A recorded positive payment renders the entire Payments accounting view unusable (crash) for that year, and the underlying validation gap lets an untyped non-zero payment persist despite the explicit guard meant to forbid it.

verdict.reasoning:
I traced the entire chain against current code on disk and every link holds.

1. VALIDATION BYPASS (real): rentmanager.ts:820 wraps the "type required when amount>0" throw (821-825) inside `if (p?.type !== undefined && p.type !== null)`. A PATCH body payment with `amount:100` and no `type` (or `type:null`) makes 820 false, so the throw is skipped. The other top-level validations in `updateByTerm` (718-724) never check per-payment type, so nothing else catches it.

2. PERSISTENCE (real): the storage map filters payments by amount only (1053: `>= 0.01`), so the untyped 100-amount payment survives, and line 1108 writes `type: payment.type || ''` → `''`. tenant.ts:142 stores rents as Mixed, so there is no schema default/required to normalize type — '' persists.

3. RENDER CRASH (real): accountingmanager.ts:318-323 passes `type` straight through into `accountingData.settlements`; the accounting page (`[year].js:101-104`) only filters by tenant name, never touching type. TenantSettlements.js:158 renders the row because amount(100)>0, then line 167 executes `t(type[0].toUpperCase() + type.slice(1))`. With type==='' , `''[0]` is undefined and `undefined.toUpperCase()` throws a TypeError, crashing the Payments tab render for that year (error boundary / blank tab).

I verified the precise byte-level structure of the guard (the throw is genuinely nested under the undefined/null check, not a sibling), confirmed the live route path `PATCH /rents/payment/:id/:term → updateByTerm → _updateByTerm` carries raw `paymentData.payments` into the bypassable loop, confirmed there is no schema-level type enforcement, and confirmed the render line has no null guard. The date guard (962-1032) is satisfiable with a valid in-term date, so it does not block the attack. Both the 'type omitted' and 'type:null' variants reach the same '' persistence. This is not a misread or a historical-fixed issue; the bug ships in current code. Severity is medium as the reviewer states: a single crafted/legacy untyped positive payment renders the entire year's Payments accounting tab uninteractable, and the explicit type-required guard is silently bypassed for the omitted/null case.

Minimal leak location: rentmanager.ts:820 — the required-type check must also fire when type is undefined/null and amount>0 (i.e. treat missing/null type as '' for the purpose of the amount>0 guard), OR defensively normalize at storage (1108) plus harden the render (TenantSettlements.js:167 with a `type ? ... : fallback` guard).

broken.title: On-screen settlement month names captured at module-load from default ('en') moment locale while CSV month headers use realm locale — Greek realm shows English month rows but Greek dates
broken.line: 13 (const months = moment.localeData().months() — module-level) and 122/141 (monthName render) vs server CSV header months from realm.locale at services/api/src/managers/accountingmanager.ts:480 + _app.js:64 (moment.locale set only inside render body)
broken.brokenShape: TenantSettlements.js line 13 evaluates moment.localeData().months() at module import time, capturing whatever locale moment had then. _app.js sets moment.locale(__lang) inside the MyApp render function body (line 64), not at module top-level, so the module-level months[] constant can bind to the default 'en' locale. The per-payment date at line 164/229 uses moment(date).format('L') at render time and DOES pick up the realm locale, so a Greek (el) realm can show English month-row labels ('January'…'December') next to Greek-formatted dates, while the settlements CSV header (server-side, realm.locale at accountingmanager.ts:480) renders Greek month names ('Ιανουάριος'…). On-screen month labels and CSV column headers therefore disagree in locale.
broken.trigger: Greek (el) realm, open Accounting → Payments: the 12 month rows render with English names while dates render in el format; the downloaded Payments CSV column headers are in Greek — on-screen vs CSV label mismatch.
broken.moneyImpact: No money mis-stated; localisation defect — an el realm sees English month labels on a money surface and the CSV header locale diverges from the on-screen labels.

verdict.codeEvidence:
TenantSettlements.js:13 `const months = moment.localeData().months();` — module-level const, evaluated ONCE at import time, never re-derived per realm locale.
TenantSettlements.js:122 `const monthName = months[month][0].toUpperCase() + months[month].slice(1);` and :141 `{monthName}` — on-screen month-ROW labels come solely from this frozen const.
TenantSettlements.js:164 `{moment(date).format('L')}` and :229 `{moment(settlement.beginDate).format('L')}` — per-payment dates / contract range format at RENDER time, so they DO pick up the realm locale set by _app.js:64.
_app.js:64 `moment.locale(pageProps?.__lang ?? 'en');` — runs inside the MyApp render BODY (after all module-level code has already executed).
_app.js:2-6 `import 'moment/locale/fr'; ... import 'moment/locale/el'; import 'moment/locale/es';` — importing a moment locale file is a side-effect that sets the global locale to the just-loaded one; the LAST import is `es` (line 6).
accountingmanager.ts:480 `const months = moment.localeData(realm.locale).months();` — server CSV header is explicitly keyed to realm.locale (Greek for an el realm).
accountingmanager.ts:288/301/317 — the on-screen JSON path returns `settlements` as a NUMERICALLY-indexed array (no month-name strings), confirming the UI label is the client const, not server-provided.
Runtime check: `require('moment/locale/fr'); ...; require('moment/locale/es')` leaves `moment.locale()` === 'es', months[0..2] === ['enero','febrero','marzo']. `moment.localeData('el').months()` === ['Ιανουάριος','Φεβρουάριος','Μάρτιος'].
verdict.reasoning:
The STRUCTURAL defect is real and present in current code: TenantSettlements.js:13 captures month names into a module-level const that is frozen at first import, BEFORE _app.js:64 ever calls moment.locale(realm). So the on-screen month-row labels (lines 122/141) do NOT track the realm locale, while (a) the per-payment dates (line 164) and contract range (line 229) DO — they format at render time after moment.locale(el) runs — and (b) the CSV header is built server-side from moment.localeData(realm.locale) (accountingmanager.ts:480), i.e. Greek for an el realm. Result: an el realm shows month-ROW labels in a different locale than its own dates and than the CSV column headers. This is a genuine localisation divergence on a money surface, exactly as the reviewer's IMPACT describes.

However the reviewer's specific DETAIL is WRONG: the const does NOT bind to 'en'. _app.js lines 2-6 import five moment locale files as side effects, and the documented behaviour of moment is that loading a locale file switches the active global locale to it. The LAST import is `import 'moment/locale/es'` (line 6), so after _app's module evaluation the global locale is `es` (Spanish), and the module-level months[] captures Spanish names. I verified this empirically with require() ordering: the global locale ends at 'es' with months ['enero','febrero','marzo']. _app does not statically import the page/TenantSettlements, so _app's locale imports always run first; there is no realistic client path where months[] is 'en'. Therefore an el realm sees SPANISH month-row labels (not English) next to Greek dates, while the CSV header is Greek.

Verdict BROKEN because the core finding (module-load capture vs render-time/realm locale → on-screen labels diverge from CSV header and from sibling dates) holds against code I read; the wrong locale value ('en' vs the actual 'es') is a correction, not a refutation, and does not change severity (low — cosmetic/localisation, no money mis-stated).
verdict.correctedDetail: The captured locale is NOT 'en'. moment's locale-file imports in _app.js:2-6 each set the global locale as a side effect; the LAST one is `import 'moment/locale/es'` (line 6), so the module-level `const months` in TenantSettlements.js:13 captures SPANISH month names ('Enero','Febrero',...). An el realm therefore renders Spanish month-row labels (lines 122/141) alongside Greek-formatted dates (lines 164/229) and a Greek CSV header (accountingmanager.ts:480) — a three-way locale divergence, not the two-way en-vs-el divergence the reviewer described. Minimal leak/fix location: move month-name derivation inside the component at render time (e.g. `const months = moment.localeData().months()` computed inside SettlementList/TenantSettlements after _app has set the locale), or pass localized month labels from the server JSON path the same way the CSV path keys them by realm.locale, instead of the module-level const at line 13.

broken.title: Rent-call email line-item table can NEVER sum to its own printed Total whenever the tenant has VAT, carried balance, debts, or a discount — the email under-states or mis-adds, and diverges from the sibling PDF which reconciles
broken.line: 23-32 (rows: preTaxAmounts L23-25, charges L26-28, buildingCharges L29-31; Total=grandTotal L32). body_text.ejs:7-15 has the identical defect.
broken.brokenShape: The email itemized table renders rows ONLY for rent.preTaxAmounts + rent.charges + rent.buildingCharges, then prints a bold 'Total' row = rent.total.grandTotal. But grandTotal = preTaxAmount + charges + buildingChargesTotal + debts - discount + vat + balance (services/api/src/businesslogic/tasks/7_total.ts:64-67). VAT (rent.vats, populated per-line at 4_vats.ts:29-83), debts (2_debts.ts), discounts, and carried Previous-balance (5_balance.ts:17-20) get NO row in the email. The sibling PDF for the SAME tenant.rents[0] renders all of them: invoicebody.ejs lists discounts (L75-82) + debts (L84-91), and rentcalltotal.ejs renders the VAT line (L9-10), Previous balance line (L15-16), then grandTotal (L21) — so PDF rows reconcile to grandTotal while the email rows do not. A VAT-charging commercial tenant is the common case: rent 1000 + 24% VAT → email shows a single 1.000,00 € 'Rent' row but a Total of 1.240,00 €, appearing to mis-add by the entire VAT.
broken.trigger: Send a rent-call (POST /emailer templateName=rentcall) for any tenant whose contract has vatRate>0, OR who carries an unpaid prior-term balance, OR has a settlement/extra-charge debt, OR a discount. The table-render gate (body_html.ejs:21) fires whenever charges.length>=1 or preTaxAmounts.length>1 or buildingCharges.length>=1, so e.g. a single-property tenant with one rent.charges line and 24% VAT renders the table and shows visible rows summing to less than the printed Total.
broken.moneyImpact: The tenant-facing rent-call email shows an itemized breakdown that does not add up to the headline amount due. For a VAT tenant the visible lines undershoot the Total by the full VAT (e.g. ~240 € on a 1.000 € rent at 24%); for a tenant carrying a balance the lines undershoot by the carried debt. Tenants reading the email distrust the figure or dispute it; the email also disagrees line-for-line with the attached PDF for identical data.

L28 <% }); %> L29 <% (rent.buildingCharges || []).forEach(function(item) { %> ... item.amount ... L31 <% }); %> L32 L33
...<%= item.description %>...<%- _.formatNumber(item.amount, 'currency') %>
<%- _.t('Total') %>...<%- _.formatNumber(rent.total.grandTotal, 'currency') %>
L34 <% } %> body_text.ejs L5-16 is the identical structure (preTaxAmounts L7-9, charges L10-12, buildingCharges L13-15; no VAT/debts/discount/balance row; gate L6 same as html L21). grandTotal definition — services/api/src/businesslogic/tasks/7_total.ts L64-67: const grandTotal = Math.round( (preTaxAmount + charges + buildingChargesTotal + debts - discount + vat + (rent.total.balance || 0)) * 100 ) / 100; VAT lives in a SEPARATE array — services/api/src/businesslogic/tasks/4_vats.ts L29-83 push entries into rent.vats[] (per preTaxAmount L29-37, per charge L39-47, settlement debts L64-73, discounts L75-83). Debts/discounts/balance are likewise separate (rent.debts[], rent.discounts[], rent.total.balance). None of vats/debts/discounts/balance are members of preTaxAmounts/charges/buildingCharges — the only three arrays the email iterates. Sibling PDF reconciles — services/pdfgenerator/templates/partials/invoicebody.ejs lists discounts (L75-82) and debts (L84-91); services/pdfgenerator/templates/partials/rentcalltotal.ejs renders "Total before VAT"=subTotal (L4), VAT line (L6-12), Previous balance line (L13-17), then "Total with VAT"=grandTotal (L18-22). So PDF visible lines sum to grandTotal; the email's do not. Data source — services/emailer/src/emailparts/data/invoice/index.ts L14-54: rents come straight from the persisted Occupant doc (dbTenant.toObject(), filtered to the term), i.e. the computed rent with vats/debts/discounts/balance populated as siblings. rentcall data wraps Invoice.get() (services/emailer/src/emailparts/data/rentcall/index.ts L18). No code path in services/emailer mutates rent.preTaxAmounts/charges/buildingCharges to fold in VAT/debts/balance before render (grep of emailer src outside data/rentcall+data/invoice returns nothing). formatNumber (services/emailer/src/utils/templatefunctions.ts L12-19) renders real Intl currency, so the rows show concrete numbers that visibly undershoot the printed Total.
verdict.reasoning:
The claim is real in current code. The rent-call email's itemized table (body_html.ejs L23-31, body_text.ejs L7-15) renders rows for ONLY rent.preTaxAmounts, rent.charges, and rent.buildingCharges, then prints a bold Total = rent.total.grandTotal (html L32 / text omits but headline L4 uses grandTotal). I verified against the actual pipeline that grandTotal = preTaxAmount + charges + buildingChargesTotal + debts - discount + vat + balance (7_total.ts:64-67), and that vat, debts, discount, and balance live in SEPARATE rent arrays/fields (rent.vats populated at 4_vats.ts:29-83; rent.debts; rent.discounts; rent.total.balance) — none of which the email iterates. So for any reachable case the table necessarily fails to sum to its own Total.

Reachability of the render gate (body_html.ejs:21 / body_text.ejs:6): it fires when buildingCharges.length>=1 OR preTaxAmounts.length>1 OR charges.length>=1. Concrete leaking scenarios confirmed:
- VAT-charging commercial tenant with at least one rent.charges line (the reviewer's qualified single-property example): gate true via charges.length; table shows rent + charge rows summing to the net, but Total = grandTotal includes ~24% VAT → visible mis-add by the full VAT.
- Multi-property tenant (preTaxAmounts.length>1) with any vatRate>0: gate true; same defect.
- Any tenant with charges/buildingCharges who also carries a prior-term balance (5_balance), a settlement/extra-charge debt (2_debts), or a discount: those add to grandTotal but get no row.

The sibling PDF for identical data reconciles (invoicebody.ejs L75-91 + rentcalltotal.ejs L4/L9-10/L15-16/L21), so the two documents disagree line-for-line. The note about the plain single-property no-charges VAT tenant: the gate is FALSE there (preTaxAmounts.length===1, no charges/buildingCharges), so no table renders — only the headline (correct) grandTotal shows; the reviewer correctly qualified their single-property example with "one rent.charges line", which is accurate. I found no guard, transformation, or historical fix that prevents the omission; the templates are used directly and no emailer code injects vat/debts/balance into the three iterated arrays. Verdict BROKEN.

Minimal leak location: body_html.ejs L23-32 and body_text.ejs L7-15 — the table emits only preTaxAmounts/charges/buildingCharges then jumps to grandTotal, with no rows for rent.vats / rent.debts / rent.discounts (negative) / rent.total.balance (and no subTotal line like the PDF's rentcalltotal.ejs). Minimal fix: add the missing rows (or render the subTotal + VAT + balance block as the PDF does) so the email's visible lines reconcile to grandTotal.

broken.title: Reminder and last-reminder dunning emails bill the FULL gross grandTotal with no subtraction of the term's own payments — over-dunning any tenant who partially paid, and diverging from the landlord UI's 'Owed remaining'
broken.line: 22 ('...proceed to the payment of {{amount}}' = grandTotal). rentcall_last_reminder/body_html.ejs:30 ('current amount of unpaid rents is {{amount}}' = grandTotal).
broken.brokenShape: Both dunning bodies quote tenant.rents[0].total.grandTotal as the amount the tenant must pay. grandTotal (7_total.ts:64-67) does NOT subtract rent.total.payment (payment is computed separately at 7_total.ts:52-69 and never deducted from grandTotal). invoice/index.ts:52-54 filters rents to the dunned term, so rents[0].total.grandTotal is the full gross term obligation even after a partial payment. The landlord's own UI computes the opposite: RentTable.js:198-200 'Owed remaining = grandTotal - paid' and RentSelector.js:16-18 '_remaining = max(0, totalAmount - payment)'.
broken.trigger: A tenant pays part of a term (e.g. owes 1.000, pays 600), then the landlord triggers a reminder or last-reminder email (POST /emailer templateName=rentcall_reminder | rentcall_last_reminder). The email says 'proceed to the payment of 1.000,00 €' / 'current amount of unpaid rents is 1.000,00 €' while the actual remaining is 400 € (as the landlord UI shows).
broken.moneyImpact: Legal dunning notices (the last_reminder is an explicit pre-eviction notice) demand the gross term amount rather than the remaining balance, over-billing every partially-paid tenant by the amount already paid. This is a tenant-facing money error in a legally-sensitive eviction-warning email and contradicts the figure the landlord sees in the rent grid for the same tenant/term.

verdict.codeEvidence: services/emailer/src/emailparts/contents/rentcall_reminder/body_html.ejs:22 — `_.t('We would be grateful if you could proceed to the payment of {{amount}} very shortly.', { amount: _.formatNumber(tenant.rents[0].total.grandTotal, 'currency') })`. services/emailer/src/emailparts/contents/rentcall_last_reminder/body_html.ejs:30 — `_.t('So far, one or more rents have not been paid. The current amount of unpaid rents is {{amount}}.', { amount: _.formatNumber(tenant.rents[0].total.grandTotal, 'currency') })`. (Same in both body_text.ejs variants — confirmed via grep, no `grandTotal - payment` / `remaining` anywhere in services/emailer/src.) services/api/src/businesslogic/tasks/7_total.ts:52-69 — `payment` is summed (52-57) and stored separately as `rent.total.payment = payment;` (69). grandTotal (64-67) = `preTaxAmount + charges + buildingChargesTotal + debts - discount + vat + (rent.total.balance||0)` — the current term's own `payment` is NEVER subtracted. services/api/src/businesslogic/tasks/5_balance.ts:17-19 — `balance = previousRent.total.grandTotal - previousRent.total.payment`. This only nets out the PRIOR term's payment as carry-in; it does not touch the dunned term's own payment. services/emailer/src/emailparts/data/invoice/index.ts:52-54 — `tenant.rents = tenant.rents.filter((rent) => rent.term === Number(params.term))`, so `rents[0]` IS the dunned term; its grandTotal is gross-of-this-term's-payment. The term comes from caller `params` (routes.ts:14 `const { templateName, recordId, params } = req.body;`), so the landlord can dun a partially-paid term. services/emailer/src/utils/templatefunctions.ts:12-19 — `formatNumber` only runs `Intl.NumberFormat(...).format(value)`; no remaining/payment logic hides there. Landlord UI (the divergence): webapps/landlord/src/components/rents/RentTable.js:198-200 — `const grandTotal = Number(rent.totalAmount)||0; const paid = Number(rent.payment)||0; const remaining = grandTotal - paid;`. webapps/landlord/src/components/payment/RentSelector.js:16-18 — `const _gt = Number(rentAmounts?.totalAmount)||0; const _pd = Number(rentAmounts?.payment)||0; const _remaining = Math.max(0, Math.round((_gt - _pd)*100)/100);`.
verdict.reasoning: I independently traced the full path and the claim holds. (1) The two cited EJS lines (plus their body_text.ejs twins) quote `tenant.rents[0].total.grandTotal` as the amount the tenant must pay. (2) grandTotal in 7_total.ts is computed WITHOUT subtracting the current term's `payment` (which is stored separately on `rent.total.payment` at line 69). The only payment-netting in the pipeline is 5_balance.ts's carry-in, which nets the PRIOR term's payment, not the dunned term's. (3) invoice/index.ts filters `rents` to `params.term`, so `rents[0]` is exactly the dunned term, gross of its own payment. Scenario: tenant owes 1.000 for term T, pays 600 against T; grandTotal[T]=1.000, payment[T]=600 (not deducted). A reminder/last-reminder for T quotes 1.000,00 € as the amount to pay / 'current amount of unpaid rents', while the actual remaining is 400 € — exactly what the landlord's own RentTable 'Owed remaining' and RentSelector '_remaining' show (grandTotal - payment). The wording 'current amount of unpaid rents' in the pre-eviction last_reminder is explicitly the unpaid balance, which it overstates by the amount already paid. Steelman rejected: the carry-in already brings forward prior arrears net of prior payments, so the missing subtraction is real money received against this term, not an intended gross. The initial `rentcall` body using grandTotal is NOT a bug (sent before payment; gross is correct) — only the reminder/last_reminder bodies are wrong. Minimal leak location: the four reminder/last-reminder template expressions; fix is `Math.max(0, grandTotal - tenant.rents[0].total.payment)`. This is adjacent emailer-money territory not deeply probed in round 1 and is currently shipping wrong money in legally-sensitive dunning emails.
verdict.correctedDetail: Confirmed in CURRENT code at HEAD. Both HTML bodies AND both body_text.ejs variants (rentcall_reminder/body_text.ejs:9, rentcall_last_reminder/body_text.ejs:15) share the defect — the fix must touch all four, not just the two HTML lines cited. The initial rentcall body (rentcall/body_html.ejs:18, body_text.ejs:4) correctly uses grandTotal and must be left alone (no payment exists yet at first call).

broken.title: Greek rent-call email renders English literals 'Total' and 'Building charges' amid otherwise-Greek copy — keys absent from el.json and not run through i18n with updateFiles:false
broken.line: 32 (_.t('Total') table footer). Building-charge fallback literal: services/api/src/businesslogic/tasks/1_base.ts:959 (description: charge.description || 'Building charges') rendered raw at body_html.ejs:30 / body_text.ejs:14.
broken.brokenShape: The table footer calls _.t('Total'); 'Total' is NOT a key in services/emailer/src/locales/el.json (verified: 71 keys, no 'Total', no 'Building charges'). i18n.configure runs with updateFiles:false (services/emailer/src/index.ts), so a missing key renders the literal English source string. The buildingCharges fallback description 'Building charges' (1_base.ts:959) is a hard-coded English string never passed through _.t() and also absent from el.json, so it prints 'Building charges' verbatim in the Greek email body.
broken.trigger: Send a rent-call to a Greek-locale realm where the breakdown table renders (any tenant matching the body_html.ejs:21 gate). The bold amount-summary row reads English 'Total' above the figure; any building charge lacking an explicit description shows 'Building charges' in English, inside an otherwise Greek email.
broken.moneyImpact: No wrong number, but the money label above the headline amount and a building-charge line render in English for Greek-locale tenants — unprofessional and inconsistent with the fully-localized PDF (which uses _.t() for its 'Total with VAT' / type labels).

verdict.reasoning:
The claim HOLDS as a real (low-severity) finding. I independently opened every cited file and the line numbers match disk exactly at HEAD f6f75966.

Mechanism verified end-to-end: _.t delegates to i18n.__ (templatefunctions.ts:9-11); i18n runs with updateFiles:false (index.ts:25); the i18n library returns the source string when the active locale lacks the key; el.json (read in full) has neither "Total" nor "Building charges". Therefore for a Greek-locale realm, body_html.ejs:32 emits the literal English "Total" above the headline amount.

broken.title: Empty post-filter rents[] crashes every rentcall/reminder email (guard checks the wrong array, then templates deref rents[0].total.grandTotal)
broken.line: invoice/index.ts:22 (guard `if (!dbTenant.rents.length)`) + :52-54 (filter to params.term); rentcall body_html.ejs:18 & :20 & :32; rentcall_reminder body_html.ejs:22 + body_text.ejs:9; rentcall_last_reminder body_html.ejs:30 + body_text.ejs:15
broken.brokenShape: invoice/index.ts:22 guards on `dbTenant.rents.length` — the FULL ledger BEFORE the term filter. Lines 52-54 then `tenant.rents = tenant.rents.filter(rent => rent.term === Number(params.term))`. When the tenant has rents but NONE for `params.term`, the post-filter array is `[]`, the guard already passed, and `tenant.rents[0]` is undefined. All three reminder data builders reuse `Invoice.get` (rentcall_reminder/index.ts and rentcall_last_reminder/index.ts both `export const get = Rentcall.get`). Every rentcall/reminder/last-reminder body does `_.formatNumber(tenant.rents[0].total.grandTotal, 'currency')` → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'total')` (verified in node). EJS render throws → caught at emailer.ts:152-154 → ServiceError('missing content for <template>', 422). The receipt (invoice) body has no `rents[0]` deref so it survives.
broken.trigger: POST /api/v2/emails with {document:'rentcall'|'rentcall_reminder'|'rentcall_last_reminder', tenantIds:[id], terms:[T]} (or year/month → defaultTerm) where term T is outside the tenant's materialized rent window. Rents exist only for terms in [begin, termination||end] (contract.ts:57-73 loop). A terminated tenant (rents stop at termination) requested for a later month, a future-month rentcall before the lease begins, or any direct/automated caller passing a term with no rent record → 422, no email sent. The guard is structurally checking the wrong array.
broken.moneyImpact: Landlord believes a payment notice / dunning reminder was sent for an outstanding term; it silently 422s instead. Tenant is never notified; rent goes uncollected. For rentcall_last_reminder this is the pre-eviction notice — a missed send can break the legal eviction timeline.

Error path: services/emailer/src/emailcontent.ts:47-50 renders body_html.ejs; reject bubbles to services/emailer/src/emailer.ts:152-154 — `} catch (error) {\n logger.error('error getting content:', error);\n throw new ServiceError(\`missing content for ${templateName}\`, 422);`. Trigger w/o validation: services/api/src/managers/emailmanager.ts:189 — `const term = Number((terms && terms[index]) || defaultTerm);` then :206 `await _sendEmail(req, { ..., term })` — no check the tenant has a rent for that term. Rent window: services/api/src/managers/contract.ts:59-73 — `while (current.isSameOrBefore(momentTermination || momentEnd, ...)) { ... contract.rents.push(rent); ... current.add(1, ...); }` — rents materialized only inside [begin, termination||end]. Devs knew Invoice.get throws on no-rents: services/emailer/src/emailparts/data/lease_expiry_notice/index.ts:102-104 wraps it — `try {\n return await Invoice.get(tenantId, params);\n } catch (err) {` with comment "Invoice.get throws when there are no rent rows" — but the rentcall/reminder paths have no such guard.
verdict.reasoning:
I independently opened every file and the line numbers match disk. The chain is fully reachable:

1. invoice/index.ts:22 guards on dbTenant.rents.length (full ledger, pre-filter), then :52-54 filters to params.term, which can leave rents=[] while the guard already passed. This is structurally checking the wrong array — the guard cannot catch an empty post-filter result.

2. All three doc types (rentcall, rentcall_reminder, rentcall_last_reminder) reuse Invoice.get (the two reminder builders literally `export const get = Rentcall.get`, and Rentcall.get calls Invoice.get). Every body_html.ejs AND body_text.ejs derefs tenant.rents[0].total.grandTotal.

3. formatNumber is a plain Intl wrapper, not safe-access; the deref `tenant.rents[0].total` happens during EJS expression evaluation and throws TypeError on undefined. The render reject is caught at emailer.ts:152 and re-thrown as ServiceError('missing content for <template>', 422). No email is sent.

4. Trigger requires no malformed input: emailmanager.ts:189 forwards an arbitrary term (from terms[] or year/month→defaultTerm) with zero validation that the tenant has a materialized rent for it. contract.ts:59-73 only materializes rents inside [begin, termination||end], so a terminated tenant requested for a later month, a future-term rentcall before lease begins, or any automated caller passing an out-of-window term reaches the empty-post-filter path.

5. The lease_expiry_notice builder wraps Invoice.get in try/catch specifically because it throws on no-rents — proof the failure mode is known, yet the rentcall/reminder paths were left unguarded.

The invoice (receipt) body has no rents[0] deref so it survives, consistent with the reviewer's note. The only correction: the title's "crashes EVERY rentcall/reminder email" overstates it — the in-window common case works; the bug fires only for out-of-window terms. But the defect, the wrong-array guard, the 422-instead-of-send outcome, and the pre-eviction-notice severity for rentcall_last_reminder are all accurate. Minimal fix: move the empty-check to AFTER the term filter (or re-check tenant.rents.length post-filter and throw a clear 422/handle gracefully) so the guard reflects the array the templates actually consume.
