broken.trigger: Tenant partially pays the current term (e.g. pays 300 of a 500 rent), then the landlord sends a rentcall_reminder or rentcall_last_reminder for that term. The email dunns the tenant for the full 500 ('current amount of unpaid rents is 500,00 €') instead of the 200 remaining.
broken.moneyImpact: Tenant is dunned (and, for last-reminder, threatened with eviction) for money they already partially paid. Over-statement of debt on a legal pre-eviction notice; tenant disputes / refuses to pay the inflated figure.

verdict.codeEvidence: VERIFIED at HEAD f6f75966 (branch nas); all line numbers match disk. (1) Template binding — gross grandTotal, payment never subtracted: - services/emailer/src/emailparts/contents/rentcall_reminder/body_html.ejs:22 — `_.t('We would be grateful if you could proceed to the payment of {{amount}} very shortly.', { amount: _.formatNumber(tenant.rents[0].total.grandTotal, 'currency') })` - rentcall_reminder/body_text.ejs:9 — same `{ amount: _.formatNumber(tenant.rents[0].total.grandTotal, 'currency') }` - rentcall_last_reminder/body_html.ejs:30 — `_.t('So far, one or more rents have not been paid. The current amount of unpaid rents is {{amount}}.', { amount: _.formatNumber(tenant.rents[0].total.grandTotal, 'currency') })` - rentcall_last_reminder/body_text.ejs:15 — same. (2) grandTotal excludes the current term's own payment — services/api/src/businesslogic/tasks/7_total.ts:64-69: ``` const grandTotal = Math.round( (preTaxAmount + charges + buildingChargesTotal + debts - discount + vat + (rent.total.balance || 0)) * 100 ) / 100; rent.total.grandTotal = Number.isFinite(grandTotal) ? grandTotal : 0; rent.total.payment = payment; ``` `payment` (lines 52-57) is stored separately and is NOT in the grandTotal sum. It is netted only into the NEXT term's carry-in: 5_balance.ts:17-19 `const balance = (Number(previousRent.total.grandTotal)||0) - (Number(previousRent.total.payment)||0);` (3) Pipeline test proving grandTotal is gross — __tests__/rent.test.js:414-416: `// grandTotal = 1000 + 100 + 75 - 75 + 102.5 + 200 = 1402.5` ; `expect(rent.total.grandTotal).toBe(1402.5)` ; `expect(rent.total.payment).toBe(900)` — grandTotal NOT reduced by the 900 paid. (4) rents[0] is exactly the requested term, read from DB un-recomputed — data/rentcall_reminder/index.ts:1-3 and data/rentcall_last_reminder/index.ts:1-3 both `export const get = Rentcall.get`; rentcall/index.ts:18 calls `Invoice.get`; invoice/index.ts:26 `const tenant = dbTenant.toObject()` then :52-54 `tenant.rents = tenant.rents.filter(rent => rent.term === Number(params.term))`. (5) No payment/status gate on send — routes.ts:13-56 `_send` permits rentcall_reminder/rentcall_last_reminder unconditionally; no remaining-due field exists in emailer/pdfgenerator (grep for newBalance/remainingAmount/amountDue/grandTotal-payment returned nothing).
verdict.reasoning: The claim holds. Trace: landlord sends a reminder for term T. The data builder (rentcall_reminder -> rentcall.get -> Invoice.get) filters tenant.rents to exactly the term-T record straight from the DB (toObject, no recompute). The template renders tenant.rents[0].total.grandTotal. Per 7_total.ts the stored grandTotal = preTaxAmount + charges + buildingCharges + debts - discount + vat + balance, and the current term's own payment is stored separately (rent.total.payment) and is NEVER subtracted from grandTotal — it nets out only into the FOLLOWING term's balance (5_balance.ts). The pipeline unit test confirms grandTotal=1402.5 while payment=900 with grandTotal not reduced. So if a tenant pays 300 of a 500 term and the landlord reminds for that same term, the reminder demands the full 500 (plus any prior carry-in via balance) instead of the 200 residual. The remaining-due (grandTotal - total.payment) is computed-available but never used by either template, and there is no send-side gate that suppresses reminders for partially-paid terms. This over-states debt on a dunning notice and, for the last-reminder, on a pre-eviction notice. Not round-1 territory (this is the emailer dunning-string surface, not the tenant payment dialog or pipeline math), not already guarded, not a misread — line numbers match disk exactly. Minimal leak: the four template bindings should quote `tenant.rents[0].total.grandTotal - tenant.rents[0].total.payment` (the residual) rather than the gross grandTotal.

broken.title: Greek rent-call email prints English 'Total' (and 'Building charges') money labels — untranslated key falls through verbatim

broken.brokenShape: rentcall body_html.ejs:32 renders the money-table footer as `<%- _.t('Total') %>`. broken.trigger: Realm locale='el' (the user's own realm). Send any rent-call email where the rent has more than one preTaxAmount, or any charge, or any buildingCharge (the `if` at body_html.ejs:21 that gates the table). verdict.codeEvidence: services/emailer/src/emailparts/contents/rentcall/body_html.ejs:32 — `<%- _.t('Total') %><%- _.formatNumber(rent.total.grandTotal, 'currency') %>` (the grand-total footer label). broken.line: 23-32 (table rows = preTaxAmounts + charges + buildingCharges; footer row 32 = rent.total.grandTotal)
broken.brokenShape: The email money table lists ONLY preTaxAmounts (line 23-25), charges (26-28), and buildingCharges (29-31), then prints a bold 'Total' row equal to `rent.total.grandTotal` (line 32). broken.moneyImpact: Tenant-facing payment demand whose itemization contradicts its own total — looks like a billing error on the landlord's part; erodes trust and triggers disputes. The amount demanded (grandTotal) is itself correct vs the PDF, but the email's own breakdown undercounts it.

verdict.codeEvidence: services/emailer/src/emailparts/contents/rentcall/body_html.ejs renders an itemized money table whose rows are ONLY preTaxAmounts + charges + buildingCharges, then prints grandTotal as the bold Total: L21: <% if ((rent.buildingCharges && rent.buildingCharges.length) || (rent.preTaxAmounts && rent.preTaxAmounts.length > 1) || (rent.charges && rent.charges.length)) { %> L23: <% rent.preTaxAmounts.forEach(function(item) { %> L26: <% (rent.charges || []).forEach(function(item) { %> L29: <% (rent.buildingCharges || []).forEach(function(item) { %> L32: ...<%- _.t('Total') %>...<%- _.formatNumber(rent.total.grandTotal, 'currency') %> No row exists for balance, discount, vat, or debts. grandTotal is NOT just preTaxAmount+charges+buildingCharges — services/api/src/businesslogic/tasks/7_total.ts:64-67: const grandTotal = Math.round( (preTaxAmount + charges + buildingChargesTotal + debts - discount + vat + (rent.total.balance || 0)) * 100 ) / 100; balance is the carried prior-term debt — services/api/src/businesslogic/tasks/5_balance.ts:17-20: const balance = (Number(previousRent.total.grandTotal) || 0) - (Number(previousRent.total.payment) || 0); The PDF, by contrast, DOES itemize those terms: - services/pdfgenerator/templates/partials/rentcalltotal.ejs:13-17 renders a "Previous balance" line (rent.total.balance) and L6-12 a VAT line. - services/pdfgenerator/templates/partials/invoicebody.ejs:75-82 renders discount rows, L84-91 debt rows. Data availability confirmed: 1_base.ts:22-40 (Rent interface total{} carries balance/preTaxAmount/charges/debts/discount/vat/grandTotal); emailer rentcall data (services/emailer/src/emailparts/data/rentcall/index.ts) loads the full occupant via Invoice.get(), so rent.total.balance/discount/vat are present in the template scope but never rendered. verdict.reasoning: I independently opened all five files and the line numbers match disk. The rent-call email body (body_html.ejs) renders an itemized table containing ONLY preTaxAmounts (L23-25), charges (L26-28), and buildingCharges (L29-31), then prints a bold Total equal to rent.total.grandTotal (L32). But 7_total.ts:64-67 defines grandTotal = preTaxAmount + charges + buildingChargesTotal + debts − discount + vat + balance, and 5_balance.ts:17-20 makes balance nonzero for any tenant carrying an unpaid prior-term amount. The email renders no balance row, no discount row, no VAT row, and no debts row, so whenever any of those is nonzero the visible rows do not sum to the printed Total. The contrast the reviewer cites is real: the PDF templates (rentcalltotal.ejs:13-21 Previous balance + Total with VAT; invoicebody.ejs:75-91 discount + debt rows) DO render those lines, so the PDF reconciles while the email does not. The data is present in template scope (Invoice.get loads the full occupant.rents[]), so it is a render omission, not missing data. This is round-2 territory (emailer money strings), not the round-1 tenant payment dialog. SCOPE CAVEAT lowering practical severity: the table is conditionally rendered (L21) only when there is a buildingCharge, >1 preTaxAmount, or any charge — so a bare single-property rent carrying only a balance shows no table and no visible mismatch; the mismatch surfaces when the table IS shown (the common building-charges / multi-property / surcharge case) AND balance/discount/vat/debts is nonzero. The reminder/last-reminder bodies print only the scalar grandTotal (no table), so they are not affected. The demanded amount (grandTotal) is itself correct; only the email's own itemization undercounts it. Real but I'd rate medium rather than high given the conditional-render gate.
verdict.correctedDetail: The reviewer's mechanism is correct, but two scope corrections: (1) The table is conditionally rendered (L21) — it does NOT appear for a single-property tenant with only a carried balance and no buildingCharges/charges/extra-preTax, so that common "carried balance" case shows no visible mismatch; the bug surfaces when the L21 condition is met AND balance/discount/vat/debts is nonzero. (2) Severity is closer to medium than high: the amount demanded is correct, only the email's internal itemization is short, and the reminder bodies (which the title also names) have no table so are unaffected. Minimal leak location: body_html.ejs:32 prints rent.total.grandTotal while L23-31 omit rows for rent.total.balance, rent.discounts/rent.total.discount, rent.vats/rent.total.vat, and rent.debts — add those rows (mirroring invoicebody.ejs:75-91 + rentcalltotal.ejs:13-21) before the Total row, or print a "subtotal of itemized lines" label instead of grandTotal.

broken.title: confirm-payment marks bills fully paid with ZERO amount reconciliation — a receipt for any amount marks a bill of any amount 'paid'; shared-RF match returns an arbitrary month's bill
broken.line: billmanager.ts:397 (rfMatch extracts only RF, no receipt amount parsed); 409-413 (findOne({realmId, rfCode, status:'pending'}) with NO .sort()); 467-477 (confirmPayment updateMany $set status:'paid' with NO comparison of any receipt amount against bill.totalAmount)
broken.brokenShape: RECONCILIATION ABSENT END-TO-END. parsePaymentReceipts (397-446) extracts ONLY the RF code from the receipt — it never parses the amount actually paid on the receipt, so there is no receipt-side figure to reconcile. confirmPayment (467-477) then flips status to 'paid' for every billId passed, with no check that the paid amount equals bill.totalAmount. Separately, findOne at 409-413 has no .sort(): when two pending bills share an rfCode (DEH reuses the RF per supply across months — bills are stored verbatim with no per-term RF uniqueness; the only unique index is (realmId,buildingId,expenseId,term), bill.ts:37), Mongo returns an arbitrary one, so the receipt can be matched to the wrong month's bill.
broken.trigger: Upload a payment-receipt PDF for a small/partial DEH payment (say 40 €) whose RF matches a 400 € pending bill (or, with multiple months sharing an RF, matches an arbitrary month). Confirm. The 400 € bill (or the wrong month) is marked fully paid with paymentDate=now.
broken.moneyImpact: A bill is recorded as fully settled when it was only partially paid (or a different month's bill is closed), so the building expense ledger shows paid-in-full for an amount that was never received. The outstanding balance silently disappears from the pending-bills tile (dashboardmanager.ts:708) — the landlord stops chasing a real debt.

verdict.codeEvidence:
All three mechanical sub-claims verified against disk (HEAD f6f75966, services/api/src/managers/billmanager.ts):

(1) parsePaymentReceipts extracts ONLY the RF code, no amount parsed — line 397:
  `const rfMatches = text.match(/RF\d{15,30}/g);`
No receipt-side amount is ever read. results.push (428-437) reports the BILL's own totalAmount (435: `totalAmount: (pendingBill as any).totalAmount`), never an amount from the receipt.

(2) findOne with NO .sort(), and rfCode is NOT uniquely indexed — billmanager.ts lines 409-413:
  `const pendingBill = await Collections.Bill.findOne({ realmId, rfCode, status: 'pending' }).lean();`
bill.ts line 37 is the only unique index: `BillSchema.index({ realmId: 1, buildingId: 1, expenseId: 1, term: 1 }, { unique: true });` — rfCode index (line 40) is non-unique. Two pending bills for the same supply across different `term`s can both carry the same rfCode; findOne without .sort() returns an arbitrary one.

(3) confirmPayment flips status to 'paid' with zero amount reconciliation — lines 462, 467-477:
  `const { billIds, paymentProofUrl } = req.body;`  (no amount field exists in the body at all)
  `const result = await Collections.Bill.updateMany({ _id: { $in: billIds }, realmId, status: 'pending' }, { $set: { status: 'paid', paymentProofUrl: ..., paymentDate: new Date(), updatedDate: new Date() } });`
No comparison of any received amount against bill.totalAmount. UI confirms it: webapps/landlord/src/components/buildings/PaymentReceiptDialog.js:64 `await confirmBillPayment(billIds);` (no amount); restcalls.js:498 `confirmBillPayment(billIds, paymentProofUrl)`. Bill schema has only `totalAmount` (bill.ts:15) — no amountPaid/paidAmount field anywhere.

IMPACT CORRECTION (the claim's one overstatement): the Bill collection does NOT feed the building expense ledger / owner liabilities / rent pipeline — businesslogic/ has no `Collections.Bill` reference (only the unrelated `ownerBilled` boolean in tasks/1_base.ts). Bill is consumed only by billmanager.list/one and dashboardmanager._fetchPendingBills (dashboardmanager.ts:709-711: `Collections.Bill.find({ realmId, status: 'pending' })`). So the real consequence is that a partially-paid (or wrong-month) bill silently drops from the pending-bills dashboard tile and shows 'paid' in the bills list — NOT a corrupted expense ledger.
verdict.reasoning:
All three code-level mechanisms in the claim are real and present at the cited lines (numbers match disk): (1) the receipt parser at 397 extracts only the RF regex and never an amount; (2) confirmPayment at 467-477 does updateMany $set status:'paid' with no amount in req.body (462) and no totalAmount comparison; (3) findOne at 409-413 has no .sort() and rfCode is not in any unique index (bill.ts:37 is the only unique index, on realmId/buildingId/expenseId/term), so a DEH RF reused across months can resolve to an arbitrary pending bill. The described trigger (upload a partial-payment receipt whose RF matches a larger pending bill, confirm, bill flips to fully paid) is exactly what the code does. This is the bill IRIS/RF auto-match surface (round-2 adjacent), not round-1 territory, and it is unguarded.

I am marking BROKEN with one impact correction: the claim says 'the building expense ledger shows paid-in-full', but the Bill collection is standalone — it does not participate in rent/owner-expense money computation. The genuine harm is narrower but still real: the only landlord-facing reminder of the outstanding obligation (the pending-bills dashboard tile, which filters status:'pending') silently drops the bill, so the landlord stops chasing a debt that was only partially paid, or a different month's bill gets closed. That is a real money-tracking defect in current shipping code, so the finding HOLDS as BROKEN; only the 'expense ledger' phrasing is wrong.
verdict.correctedDetail: Severity is better characterized as medium (not high): the defect lives entirely in the bill-tracking/pending-bills-reminder feature, which is decoupled from the rent/owner-expense money pipeline. No owner liability, rent allocation, receipt PDF, or dashboard money bucket is mis-computed. The concrete wrong outcomes are: (a) a bill is marked status:'paid' with paymentDate=now regardless of the actual amount received (no reconciliation field exists), and (b) when two pending bills share an rfCode across terms, the unordered findOne at billmanager.ts:409 can close the wrong month's bill. Both make a still-outstanding obligation vanish from dashboardmanager._fetchPendingBills (status:'pending' filter, line 709-711). Minimal fix locations: parse and return the receipt's paid amount in parsePaymentReceipts (~397), reject/flag confirm-payment when no received amount is reconciled against bill.totalAmount in confirmPayment (~467), and add a deterministic .sort() (e.g. by term/dueDate) plus billId-disambiguation when an rfCode matches multiple pending bills (~409-413).

This is not round-1 territory (bills/IRIS QR), it is currently unguarded, and the impact matches the reviewer's medium severity: no direct money error, but the IRIS-pay-by-QR feature value is lost after the import dialog closes. {t('Amount')}

broken.title: RF-code -> pending-bill match is non-deterministic (no sort); a re-used per-supply RF marks an arbitrary month's bill paid
broken.line: 408-413 (parsePaymentReceipts match loop)
broken.brokenShape: const pendingBill = await Collections.Bill.findOne({ realmId, rfCode, status: 'pending' }).lean(); — findOne with no sort returns an arbitrary document when more than one pending bill shares the rfCode. confirmBills stores rfCode verbatim with no per-term uniqueness (bill.ts index is on term, not rfCode), and ISO 11649 RF payment references for utilities are typically stable per supply/customer account across billing months.
broken.trigger: Two consecutive months' DEH bills for the same supply are both still pending (common — building bills queue up), so both rows share the identical rfCode. A receipt for one month matches whichever row Mongo returns first and confirmPayment marks that arbitrary month paid.
broken.moneyImpact: Wrong month's bill marked paid; the actually-paid month stays 'pending' and the unpaid month is hidden, corrupting the pending-bills outstanding total in either direction.

verdict.reasoning:
The claim HOLDS as a real, unguarded bug (verdict BROKEN per schema). I independently traced the full path:

1. Schema permits the dangerous state: the ONLY unique index (bill.ts:37) is (realmId,buildingId,expenseId,term). The rfCode index (bill.ts:40) is non-unique. confirmBills (billmanager.ts:300-347) saves with rfCode verbatim and only catches the term-based 11000 duplicate. Two consecutive months for the SAME supply/expense differ only in `term`, so both persist as status:'pending' sharing one identical rfCode.

2. The RF code is genuinely supply-stable, not bill-unique: deh.ts:85-86 extracts the bare ISO 11649 RF creditor reference; the amount lives in a separate paymentCode (deh.ts:90-92) that is never used for matching. So the reviewer's premise (same RF across months) is grounded in the actual parser, not just domain folklore.

3. The match is non-deterministic: parsePaymentReceipts (billmanager.ts:409-413) does Collections.Bill.findOne({realmId, rfCode, status:'pending'}) with NO .sort() and no term/amount filter. With two matching pending docs, Mongo returns one by natural/internal order — arbitrary. The chosen billId (line 432) flows to confirmPayment.updateMany (line 467) which marks THAT month paid.

4. Outcome: paying June's receipt can mark May's bill paid; June stays pending. The outstanding pending-bills total is corrupted and the genuinely-unpaid month is hidden — exactly the medium-severity money/state corruption described.

Git blame shows lines 408-413 are original (a7a95a3c, 2026-05-09) and untouched by any later fix; no sort or disambiguation was ever added. Minimal leak location: billmanager.ts:409 findOne lacks a deterministic tiebreaker (e.g., should sort by term and/or filter to the receipt's amount/term) when multiple pending bills share an rfCode.

Caveat (does not change verdict): exploit requires two same-supply same-rfCode bills both pending simultaneously. If a given utility issues a fresh RF per statement, the trigger won't fire — but the code provides no guard either way, and DEH-style supply-stable RF references are the documented norm, so the wrong-outcome path is reachable with ordinary multi-month bill queues.

broken.trigger: Tenant has monthly bill EUR500 with a EUR200 manual payment already recorded on the current term. Dialog shows 'Monthly EUR300'. User ticks Monthly and clicks Record. Server records a single EUR500 transfer dated today and the original EUR200 payment (its date/type/reference) is DELETED from rent.payments. Ledger now shows one EUR500 transfer instead of EUR200 + EUR300. The toast reports only a COUNT (ExpressPaymentDialog.js:166-184), never the amount, so the EUR200-payment loss and the EUR300-vs-EUR500 mismatch are completely silent. broken.moneyImpact: Records gross (e.g. EUR500) while user was told net (EUR300) — over-records by the prior-payment amount AND destroys the prior payment record (its date/type/reference), corrupting the ledger and the audit trail. Silent: no amount in the toast.

verdict.reasoning:
The reviewer's claim holds in CURRENT code. There are two independent, compounding defects in the express settle path and the second-opinion trace confirms both end-to-end:

(1) DISPLAY/RECORD MISMATCH (over-charge). The client derives the offered "Monthly" figure by subtracting r.payment (= rent.total.payment = sum of ALL recorded payments on the term, 7_total.ts:52-57) from the gross monthly bill (ExpressPaymentDialog.js:55-71), and renders that NET remaining (line 268). The server's bulkExpressPayment recomputes monthlyOwed purely from _computeOwedLines(targetRent), which reads only gross line items and never subtracts targetRent.payments or total.payment (rentmanager.ts:548-557, _computeOwedLines 103-189). It then records a single transfer for the full GROSS amount (596-608). With a €500 bill and a €200 payment already on the term, the dialog shows "Monthly €300" but the server records a €500 transfer. No clamp against existing payments exists anywhere in the express write path; the only total.payment reads (365, 431) are a tooltip builder and an accounting accumulator.

(2) PRIOR-PAYMENT DESTRUCTION (data loss). _updateByTerm builds settlements.payments from ONLY the incoming paymentData.payments (rentmanager.ts:797-802, 1052) and never merges the term's previously-saved occupant.rents[target].payments. Contract.payTerm then rebuilds the target term via computeRent, which re-initializes rent.payments=[] (index.ts:28) and taskPayments pushes ONLY settlements.payments (6_payments.ts:10-56); contract.ts:283-288 passes the caller's settlements straight through for the target term with no merge. The normal payment dialog avoids exactly this by sending clonedValues.payments=[...savedPayments,...drafts] (PaymentTabs.js:596); the express path sends only the one new payment. Net effect: the prior €200 payment (its date/type/reference) is overwritten by a single €500 transfer dated today.

Both effects are silent: the success toast reports only a count of writes (ExpressPaymentDialog.js:156-184), never an amount, so neither the €300-vs-€500 over-record nor the loss of the €200 payment record surfaces to the user. The route is live (routes.ts:242-244). This is not round-1 territory (tenant payment dialog merge) — the express bulk drawer is a distinct surface that reuses _updateByTerm without the caller-side merge the normal dialog performs. MINIMAL LEAK LOCATION: the missing payment-merge / net clamp in bulkExpressPayment (rentmanager.ts:548-611) — it must subtract targetRent.total.payment (or the already-paid amount per line) when computing the express amount AND include the existing targetRent.payments in paymentData.payments (mirroring PaymentTabs.js:596), since _updateByTerm/computeRent rebuild payments from scratch.

verdict.reasoning: Independently opened every cited file. The reviewer's chain holds end-to-end against current code: (a) the dialog's offered "Monthly" amount is discount-NET (totalWithoutBalanceAmount = grandTotal - balance, and grandTotal nets the discount per 7_total.ts:65); (b) the standing lease discount (occupant.discount, real field tenant.ts:147) is carried as contract.discount at rentmanager.ts:790 and pushed into the SEPARATE rent.discounts[] array by 3_discounts.ts, while preTaxAmounts stays the full gross (1_base.ts:882-888); (c) the server's _computeOwedLines (103-189) sums preTax+charges+buildingCharges+vat+debts and never subtracts rent.discounts, so monthlyOwed is the pre-discount gross; (d) the resolved gross amount is persisted verbatim (1057/1107) with no clamp against the discount-net grandTotal (the only cap at 1143-1153 governs `promo`, not the standing discount, and Express sends no promo). This is a money over-recording bug, not a tautology and not already guarded. I checked for any discount subtraction in the owed-line path and the promo cap; neither protects the standing contract discount. Minimal fix location: _computeOwedLines must net rent.discounts into the rent/preTax owed lines (mirroring how 7_total.ts subtracts discount into grandTotal) so monthlyOwed equals the displayed totalWithoutBalanceAmount.

I independently opened all five cited files at the exact lines and traced the full prop chain. The claim is accurate in current HEAD code:

- The rents page loads the entire month into `data` (no server-side pagination, no load-more on this page), then `List` chunks it into pages of 21 (`pageSize = 21`, List.js:36) and passes ONLY `chunks[safePageIndex-1]` to `renderList` (List.js:112).

This is not round-1 territory (round 1 covered the tenant payment dialog and dashboard buckets, not this bulk drawer's pagination scope). It is not guarded anywhere: the dialog is mounted in exactly one place, always fed the paginated prop. 

Severity assessment: matches the reviewer — a landlord with a building/portfolio exceeding 21 rent rows in a month opens Express on page 1, Records, sees a success toast, and believes the whole month is settled while arrears tenants on later pages remain unrecorded with no indication. No money is mis-recorded, but it directly causes silent under-collection. A correct fix would feed the dialog the full filtered list (`filteredData`) rather than the single page chunk — e.g. lift the express trigger/list source above pagination, or pass the unpaginated array to the dialog separately from the table's per-page rows.

broken.title: Express drawer promises a settlement date computed from LOCAL time but the server records it in UTC — off-by-one calendar day near midnight in Athens (UTC+2/+3)

verdict.reasoning: The claim holds against current code. The Express drawer header (ExpressPaymentDialog.js:219) renders the promised settlement date with `moment().format('DD/MM/YYYY')` (LOCAL), while the server stamps the actual `payment.date` with `moment.utc().format('DD/MM/YYYY')` (rentmanager.ts:504 used at :603). I confirmed the server response shape (results array, ~lines 640-666) contains no date field, and the client onSuccess handler (141-159) reads only skipped/failed/amount — so nothing reconciles the locally-shown header date with the UTC date persisted on the payment. On Athens time (UTC+2 winter / UTC+3 summer), between local midnight and UTC midnight (00:00-03:00 local) `moment()` and `moment.utc()` resolve to different calendar days; the header shows tomorrow's date while the payment is stamped today's UTC date, which then appears in the ledger/receipt/CSV. ExpressPaymentDialog.js:17 `import useTranslation from 'next-translate/useTranslation';` and :34 `const { t } = useTranslation('common');` — confirms next-translate is the i18n lib (package.json: "next-translate": "2.6.2").

  `var numKey = key + "_" + query.count;` → "{{count}} tenants_1" (absent → skip)
  `var pluralKey = key + "_" + pluralRules.select(query.count);` → for count=1 select() returns "one" → "{{count}} tenants_one"; `if (getDicValue(dic, pluralKey) !== undefined) return pluralKey;` (absent → skip)

locales grep (all six common.json) — base key present, NO _one variant:
  en:1140  "{{count}} tenants": "{{count}} tenants"
  el:1138  "{{count}} tenants": "{{count}} ενοικιαστές"
  fr-FR:1045 "{{count}} tenants": "{{count}} locataires"
  de-DE:1045 "{{count}} tenants": "{{count}} Mieter"
  es-CO:1045 "{{count}} tenants": "{{count}} inquilinos"

Its plural() in transCore.js, for a query with count===1, first probes "{{count}} tenants_1", then "{{count}} tenants_" + pluralRules.select(1) which is "{{count}} tenants_one". I grepped all six common.json files: the base key "{{count}} tenants" exists in every locale but NO "{{count}} tenants_one" variant exists in any of them (the immediately adjacent sibling key "{{count}} tenants imported" DOES carry a _one variant in all six — confirming the project uses next-translate plural suffixes and that this key was simply missed). When both the _1 and _one probes miss, plural() falls through to `return key`, so t() resolves the base PLURAL value and interpolates count=1, rendering "1 ενοικιαστές" (el), "1 tenants" (en), "1 locataires" (fr), etc. — grammatically wrong singular. totals.count===1 is reachable: it increments once per tenant-row with any checkbox selected (lines 100-115), so selecting exactly one tenant in the Express drawer triggers it. The claim holds against current code at f6f75966. I independently opened all files in the chain and verified every link:

The two renders live in the same flex column (RentTable.js L507-526). _remaining goes through NumberFormat → useFormatNumber → Intl.NumberFormat(locale,{style:'currency',currency}), producing el-correct "0,00 €" (comma decimal, narrow no-break space, trailing locale symbol). webapps/tenant/src/utils/formatnumber/index.ts:37-43 — getFormatNumber substitutes it for any nullish currency:
```
    return formatNumber(
      locale || DEFAULT_LOCALE,
      currency || DEFAULT_CURRENCY,   // line 39: '' or undefined -> 'USD'
      value,
```
And formatNumber feeds it to Intl.NumberFormat as the currency symbol:
index.ts:19-23 `new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: 'currency', currency: currency, minimumFractionDigits }).format(value)`

Call sites pass realm currency straight through, no normalization:
webapps/tenant/src/components/invoice-table.tsx:89 `const formatNumber = getFormatNumber(locale, lease.landlord.currency);` (used at 157 invoice.grandTotal, 189/191 invoice.payment)
webapps/tenant/src/components/contract-card.tsx:22 `const formatNumber = getFormatNumber(locale, lease.landlord.currency);` (used at 86 lease.deposit, 95 lease.balance)

Source of lease.landlord.currency is the raw realm currency with no fallback:
services/tenantapi/src/controllers/tenants.ts:125 `const landlord = tenant.realmId;`
services/tenantapi/src/controllers/tenants.ts:147-152 `landlord: { name: landlord.name, ..., currency: landlord.currency, locale: landlord.locale }`

Schema permits nullish currency (no required, no default):
services/common/src/collections/realm.ts:113-114 `locale: String,  currency: String`

Asymmetry the reviewer cites is real — landlord side defaults to EUR, not USD:
webapps/landlord/src/utils/numberformat.js:1-3 `export const formatNumber = (locale = 'en', currency = 'EUR', ...`
verdict.reasoning: The mechanism is verified exactly as described in CURRENT code at f6f75966. getFormatNumber/formatNumber hardcode a USD fallback via `currency || DEFAULT_CURRENCY` (index.ts:4,39); the `||` catches both undefined and empty string. Both call sites (invoice-table.tsx:89, contract-card.tsx:22) pass `lease.landlord.currency` directly, and that value is the raw realm currency serialized untouched by tenantapi (tenants.ts:151) — no intervening guard at any layer (dashboard page passes the fetched lease straight to the components). The Realm schema declares `currency: String` with NO `required` and NO `default` (realm.ts:114), so a realm document with a missing/empty currency is schema-valid and possible for legacy/partially-migrated/direct-DB realms. When that happens, every tenant-facing money figure (grandTotal, payment, deposit, balance) renders with a `$` symbol on euro amounts — a concrete wrong-currency render. The reviewer's distinguishing claim is also confirmed: the landlord formatter defaults to EUR (numberformat.js:3), so this USD default is an asymmetric tenant-side defect, not intended app-wide behavior. The one mitigating fact is that API-driven realm creation enforces currency via `_hasRequiredFields` (realmmanager.ts:51, 422 on missing), so a normally-created realm will carry a currency — which is why the reviewer scoped this to legacy/partial realms and rated it sev-low/latent. That mitigation does not refute the finding; it bounds the trigger to exactly the legacy/partial data state this audit targets, and the schema still permits it. The path to the wrong outcome is fully traced in code I read; this is a genuine (latent, low-severity) wrong-render defect, not a misread or already-guarded condition. Minimal fix location: change the tenant-side DEFAULT_CURRENCY at index.ts:4 to 'EUR' to match the landlord side (and the el-locale euro reality), or guard the realm currency upstream.
verdict.correctedDetail: Finding HOLDS as written, with two precision notes. (1) The fallback fires on both `undefined` AND empty string `''` because line 39 uses `||`, not a JS default parameter — broader than a default-arg would be. (2) The trigger is correctly scoped: API realm creation requires currency (realmmanager.ts:51 `_hasRequiredFields` throws 422 if `!realm.currency`), so this cannot arise from a normally-created realm; it requires a legacy/partially-migrated/direct-DB realm doc with nullish currency, which the schema (realm.ts:114, plain `String`, no required/default) permits. Severity low/latent as the reviewer states; the asymmetry vs the landlord EUR default (numberformat.js:3) is accurate and confirms intent was EUR, not USD.

broken.title: CSV formula-injection guard (_sanitizeCsvText) is wired ONLY to the in-app JSON path, never to the actual .csv download — tenant/property names and payment references reach the spreadsheet unsanitized
broken.line: 31-41 (guard def), 352-354 (only call sites, rawData=true JSON), 201-203/261-264/160 (name/reference/properties into CSV), 367-369/387-392 (settlement cell), 426-490 (the 3 *AsCsv exports)
broken.brokenShape: The accounting CSV exports build downloadable cells from free-text fields — tenant.name, tenant.reference, property name, and per-payment reference — with NO sanitization. _sanitizeCsvText (the formula-injection neutralizer whose own header comment at lines 20-30 says it defends `text/csv` exports against `=SYSTEM(...)` execution) is invoked only inside the `rawData=true` branch (lines 352-354), which produces JSON consumed by the React Accounting UI — exactly the surface where formula injection is harmless (React renders, never evaluates). Verified in Node that json2csv only double-quotes the cell, leaving the leading `=`/`+`/`-`/`@`; Excel/LibreOffice/Sheets strip the quotes and evaluate the formula. Tenant name has only length validators (validators.ts:130-253), no leading-char restriction, and AADE/E9 PDF import names are free-form, so a tenant/property literally named `=cmd|'/c calc'!A1` is accepted and lands in the downloaded CSV.

broken.moneyImpact: Formula/DDE injection into the accountant's spreadsheet from a downloaded money document; the documented security control is dead code on the path it claims to protect. No data corruption inside the app, but arbitrary-formula execution / data exfiltration on the export consumer.

broken.title: Payment-recorded success toast renders dot-decimal + glued € regardless of org locale/currency
broken.line: 649-653 (key 'Payment of {{amount}}€ recorded', amount: _sum.toFixed(2))
broken.brokenShape: After a real rent payment is recorded, the confirmation toast interpolates `_sum.toFixed(2)` (forced dot decimal) into the key 'Payment of {{amount}}€ recorded'. The el translation (locales/el/common.json:618 'Καταγράφηκε καταβολή {{amount}}€') and the en key both bake the € symbol into the string. On a Greek org every sibling amount renders '1.234,56 €' via the locale-aware NumberFormat (which PaymentTabs even imports), but this money-write confirmation renders 'Καταγράφηκε καταβολή 1234.45€' — Anglo dot decimal, no grouping, € glued to the digits, and on any non-EUR realm the € is simply the wrong currency symbol.
broken.trigger: On an org with locale='el' (or any non-en/non-EUR realm), record any rent payment > 0 → the green success toast shows the amount with a dot decimal separator and a hardcoded/wrong currency symbol.
broken.moneyImpact: Wrong-locale money rendered on a payment-write confirmation; misleading currency symbol on non-EUR realms. Display-only (the recorded value is correct) but it's the user-facing receipt of a money mutation.

verdict.codeEvidence:
PaymentTabs.js:648-653 (the money-write success toast):
```
        if (_sum > 0) {
          toast.success(
            t('Payment of {{amount}}€ recorded', {
              amount: _sum.toFixed(2)
            })
          );
```
_sum is computed at lines 613-616 as `drafts.reduce((s, p) => s + (Number(p?.amount) || 0), 0)` — a raw JS Number. `Number.prototype.toFixed(2)` ALWAYS emits a dot decimal and never groups, regardless of locale: e.g. `(1234.45).toFixed(2) === "1234.45"`.

The translation keys bake the € symbol into the literal string:
- locales/el/common.json:618  "Payment of {{amount}}€ recorded": "Καταγράφηκε καταβολή {{amount}}€"
- locales/en/common.json:618   "Payment of {{amount}}€ recorded": "Payment of {{amount}}€ recorded"
So the rendered output is `Καταγράφηκε καταβολή 1234.45€` (dot decimal, no grouping, € glued).

Contrast with the app's locale-aware path, which PaymentTabs itself imports and uses for every OTHER amount (line 29 `import NumberFormat from '../NumberFormat'`; rendered at lines 786, 826, 846, 853):
- NumberFormat.js:33,59 → useFormatNumber()
- useFormatNumber.js:11-17 → formatNumber(store.organization.selected.locale, store.organization.selected.currency, value, ...)
- numberformat.js:7-11 → `Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: 'currency', currency }).format(value)`
For an el-GR / EUR org that yields `1.234,45 €` (dot grouping, comma decimal, currency symbol from Intl).

The locale and currency are per-org configurable, so a non-EUR realm is reachable:
- services/common/src/collections/realm.ts:113-114 → `locale: String, currency: String` (free strings, no EUR/en constraint)
- LandlordForm.js:32 `locale: z.string().min(1)` — landlord picks the locale on org setup.
verdict.reasoning: The claim holds against current code. The cited lines match disk exactly (648-653). The toast for a recorded rent payment interpolates `_sum.toFixed(2)` — which is hardwired to ASCII-dot decimal with no thousands grouping — into a translation key that hardcodes the € symbol (verified in both el and en common.json at line 618). This is NOT routed through the org-locale-aware NumberFormat/useFormatNumber/Intl.NumberFormat chain that every other amount in the SAME file (lines 786/826/846/853) and across the app uses. Since Realm.locale and Realm.currency are free, per-org configurable strings (realm.ts:113-114), the wrong outcome is reachable on real data: a Greek (el-GR/EUR) org sees `Καταγράφηκε καταβολή 1234.45€` instead of the correct `1.234,45 €`, and any non-EUR realm shows the wrong currency symbol entirely. It is display-only — the recorded payment value (sent via `payRent` at line 632 using the structured `payment` object, not the toast string) is unaffected — but it is the user-facing confirmation of a money mutation, rendered in the wrong locale/currency. Severity medium is appropriate; the leak is contained to the single toast.success call at PaymentTabs.js:649-653. Not round-1 territory (round 1 covered the payment dialog's submit/guard logic and money math, not the success-toast locale rendering). Not historically guarded — there is no NumberFormat/formatNumber call on this path. Minimal fix: format `_sum` via useFormatNumber()/Intl with the org locale+currency and drop the literal € from the key.

broken.title: toOccupantData expense-sum collapses an entire property's Additional-charges to €0 when any one expense lacks a numeric amount (under-count, zeroes valid charges)
broken.brokenShape: occupant.expenses += (item.expenses?.length && item.expenses.reduce((acc,{amount})=>acc+amount,0)) || 0. The reduce has NO Number()/||0 coercion on `amount` (typed `amount: number` at line 498 but never enforced). If any single expense in the property has amount === undefined/null (schema tenant.ts:77 `amount: Number` has no default; validator occupantmanager.ts:670 only checks amount when `!== undefined && !== null && !== ''`), the reduce returns NaN, and the outer `(length && NaN) || 0` evaluates NaN as falsy → returns 0. Verified in node: expenses [{amount:100},{amount:undefined},{amount:30}] → 0 (not 130, not NaN). The whole property's legitimate expenses are wiped to zero. The engine (1_base.ts:906-909) instead maps each expense independently with Math.round((Number(amount)||0)*100)/100, so it correctly bills 100+0+30 = 130/term. RentOverviewCard renders tenant.expenses (line 32) and tenant.total (line 58); both go to €0/'—' while the rent ledger in the SAME response (rentmanager.ts:1296-1299 returns {occupant, rents}) bills 130. preTaxTotal/total/vat (503-508) all under-count by the property's full expense sum.
broken.trigger: Tenant has a property with ≥2 per-tenant expenses where one carries no amount: e.g. PATCH /api/v2/tenants/:id with properties[0].expenses = [{title:'Κοινόχρηστα',amount:100,beginDate,endDate},{title:'Legacy',beginDate,endDate}/*no amount*/,{title:'Νερό',amount:30,beginDate,endDate}]. Validator accepts it (amount checked only when present). Overview shows Additional charges €0 / Total = rent only; ledger bills €130/term. Also reachable from any legacy occupant row persisted before amount was consistently set.
broken.moneyImpact: Tenant Rental overview card (and tenant-list summary) silently reports €0 additional charges and a Total missing the full per-property expense sum, while the actual rent ledger bills the valid expenses. Landlord reading the overview under-states what the tenant owes by the whole property's expense total each month; reconciliation against the ledger row diverges with no error.

services/api/src/managers/frontdata.ts:495-501 (verified on disk, line numbers match):

496    (item.expenses?.length &&
497      item.expenses.reduce(
498        (acc: number, { amount }: { amount: number }) => acc + amount,

No Number()/||0 coercion on `amount` inside the reduce.

Schema (services/common/src/collections/tenant.ts:77): `amount: Number` — no default, not required.

Validator (services/api/src/managers/occupantmanager.ts:670): `if (e?.amount !== undefined && e.amount !== null && e.amount !== '') { validateFiniteNumber(...) }` — a missing/undefined amount is NOT validated, so the row is accepted and persisted with no amount.

Engine (services/api/src/businesslogic/tasks/1_base.ts:906-908): each expense mapped independently with `amount: Math.round((Number(amount) || 0) * 100) / 100` — bills 100 + 0 + 30 = 130.

Consumer (webapps/landlord/src/components/tenants/RentOverviewCard.js): line 32 `<NumberFormat value={tenant.expenses} />`, line 47 preTaxTotal, line 51 vat, line 58 total — all from the collapsed occupant fields.

Response coupling (services/api/src/managers/rentmanager.ts:1297): `occupant: FD.toOccupantData(dbOccupant)` shipped alongside `rents` (engine-billed) in one payload → overview €0 vs ledger €130 divergence.

Runtime proof (node): after the JSON.parse(JSON.stringify()) round-trip at frontdata.ts:398 the `amount:undefined` key is stripped → reduce returns NaN → `(3 && NaN) || 0` === 0. Confirmed: [{amount:100},{amount:undefined},{amount:30}] → 0, NOT 130.
verdict.reasoning:
The finding holds. I independently traced the full path in current HEAD code and confirmed every cited line matches disk.

Mechanism: toOccupantData computes occupant.expenses as a per-property subtotal using `item.expenses.reduce((acc,{amount})=>acc+amount, 0)` with no numeric coercion. If any single expense in a property carries no `amount` (undefined/missing — the JSON round-trip at line 398 strips the key entirely), the reduce yields NaN. The outer `(item.expenses?.length && NaN) || 0` then evaluates NaN as falsy and substitutes 0, wiping that entire property's legitimate expense sum (100 + 30 here) to €0. The rent engine (tasks/1_base.ts:906-908) maps each expense independently with `Math.round((Number(amount)||0)*100)/100`, so the SAME response bills the valid expenses (130) while the overview card reports 0 for that property's Additional charges, and preTaxTotal/vat/total all under-count by that amount.

Reachability is real: schema has no default (tenant.ts:77) and the validator only checks amount when present (occupantmanager.ts:670), so a PATCH /tenants/:id with an expense lacking `amount`, or any legacy row persisted without it, is accepted. RentOverviewCard renders the collapsed fields directly.

One precision correction to the reviewer's framing (not affecting the verdict): the NaN path fires only for `amount === undefined`/missing. A literal `null` does NOT trigger it — `acc + null` coerces to 0, so [{amount:100},{amount:null},{amount:30}] correctly yields 130 (verified in node). The reviewer's reproduction (a row with no amount key) is exactly the undefined case and is valid and reachable.

Minimal leak location: frontdata.ts:497-498 — the reduce must coerce, e.g. `(acc, { amount }) => acc + (Number(amount) || 0)`, matching the engine's coercion so the two paths agree.
verdict.correctedDetail: Reviewer's claim that `null` triggers the zero-collapse is imprecise: only an undefined/missing `amount` produces NaN→0. `null` coerces to 0 in `acc + null` and the property still totals correctly (130). The reproduction case (expense object with no `amount` key — legacy rows or a PATCH that omits amount) is the undefined case and is correct, reachable, and accepted by the validator. The under-count is per offending property's full expense sum (other properties' expenses survive), and the overview's Total/preTaxTotal/VAT all under-count by that same amount while the ledger in the same response bills it.

broken.title: toOccupantData sums every expense at full value ignoring its begin/end window — One-time charge inflates the 'recurring' monthly Total
broken.brokenShape: occupant.expenses is the UNCONDITIONAL sum of all properties[].expenses[].amount (495-501); it ignores beginDate/endDate. The authoritative engine filters each expense by its window before billing (1_base.ts:893-905: currentMoment.isBetween(expenseBegin, expenseEnd, 'months', '[]')), so a Frequency=One-time expense (begin===end, the explicit surface of this task) bills exactly ONE month, and a sub-period window (e.g. Mar–Jun) bills only those months. The overview adds the full amount to occupant.expenses → preTaxTotal (503) → total (505) → vat (507), and RentOverviewCard.js explicitly labels this as RECURRING monthly cost (comment lines 22-29; renders tenant.expenses line 32, tenant.total line 58). So a €500 one-time charge on a 12-month lease shows 'Additional charges €500' and inflates the recurring Total by €500 every month, diverging from the per-term rents[] returned in the same payload (rentmanager.ts:1296-1299).
broken.trigger: Tenant with a property expense whose window excludes the current/typical month: a One-time expense (begin===end) set via the Frequency dropdown (LeaseContractForm.js:212-216), or any custom sub-period window. Open the tenant Rental overview card → Additional charges and Total are higher than the actual rent ledger bills for any month outside the window.
broken.moneyImpact: Overview Total over-states the tenant's monthly liability by the full value of every non-recurring/out-of-window expense; the figure no longer reconciles with the rent ledger shown beside it. With VAT set, the inflated expense is also re-taxed (vat = preTaxTotal*vatRatio, line 507), compounding the over-count.

verdict.reasoning: I independently opened every cited file at the exact lines and the claim holds in CURRENT code. (1) frontdata.ts:495-501 sums item.expenses[].amount unconditionally; the only thing done with beginDate/endDate is string-formatting them (479-486) — there is no window filter before the sum, and no compensating guard anywhere in toOccupantData (read 397-526 fully). The result flows into preTaxTotal (503), total (505), and vat (507, re-taxing the inflated expense). (2) The authoritative rent engine filters the SAME per-tenant property expenses by their beginDate/endDate window via isBetween (1_base.ts:893-905), so a One-time expense (begin===end) bills exactly one term and a sub-period bills only its window — the engine's per-term rent.charges therefore diverges from the overview's full-value sum for any out-of-window term. (3) The trigger is reachable: LeaseContractForm onFrequencyChange (211-220) sets begin===end for the explicit 'One-time' option (215-216) and offers a Custom sub-period range. (4) The value is presented to the user as a RECURRING monthly cost: RentOverviewCard's own comment (22-29) states these are recurring costs paid alongside rent, and it renders tenant.expenses/tenant.total juxtaposed 1:1 with the monthly tenant.rental. (5) Both figures ship in the SAME payload (rentmanager.ts:1296-1298), and the tenant page consumes the unwindowed occupant via GET /tenants/:id -> toOccupantData -> fetchTenant -> RentOverviewCard, so the wrong number is actually displayed. Caveats that do NOT defeat the finding: for the common recurring case (empty begin/end -> full lease span via the 480-485 defaults) the sum is correct, so this is a conditional bug (medium severity, as the reviewer states), not always-on; and the reviewer's line/path citations for 1_base.ts were slightly off (right logic, /tasks/ subdir, lines 890-911). Neither changes the outcome. Minimal leak location: frontdata.ts:495-501 — the reduce must skip expenses whose [beginDate,endDate] window excludes the period being summarized (or the summary must be defined and displayed as a lifetime total, not a recurring monthly figure). The fix belongs at frontend label semantics + this reduce; the engine side (1_base.ts) is already correct.
verdict.correctedDetail: Reviewer's file/line for the engine filter is imprecise: the path is services/api/src/businesslogic/tasks/1_base.ts (note the /tasks/ subdir) and the filter is lines 890-911 (filter callback 893-905), not 1_base.ts:893-905. broken.title: Frequency dropdown flip to Monthly silently overwrites a custom sub-period expense window with the full lease range (over-bills extra months)
broken.brokenShape: onFrequencyChange unconditionally setValue's beginDate=lease begin and endDate=lease end on the 'monthly' branch (219-220), discarding any custom window the landlord set via the 'Custom date range' collapsible. Frequency is derived from begin===end (isOneTime, 201-205), so a user with a Mar–Jun expense who toggles the dropdown to 'one-time' and back to 'monthly' (or just touches it) loses the Mar–Jun bounds and expands the expense to the entire lease. On save this persists wider dates; the engine (1_base.ts:893-905) then bills the expense for every month of the lease instead of Mar–Jun.
broken.trigger: Landlord sets a custom sub-period expense window, then interacts with the per-expense Frequency Select. The Monthly branch overwrites both dates to the lease range; saving over-bills the extra months.
broken.moneyImpact: Real over-bill: an expense intended for a sub-period is silently expanded to the full lease term, charging the tenant the expense amount for additional months. Requires explicit user toggling but produces wrong money in the ledger, not just display.

verdict.reasoning: The core claim is real and unguarded in CURRENT code (HEAD f6f75966). For an existing expense with a custom Mar–Jun window (begin≠end → Select shows 'monthly'), deliberately toggling Frequency to 'one-time' and back to 'monthly' fires onValueChange twice; both branches setValue the expense dates to LEASE-derived props (beginDate/endDate are the lease range from watch, lines 325-326/502-503), wiping the Mar–Jun bounds and expanding to the full lease. _onSubmit (387-391) serializes the widened dates verbatim — no re-narrowing — and the rent engine (tasks/1_base.ts 893-905) bills the expense for every term inside the window, so the extra months are real ledger over-bills, not a display artifact. There is no guard (no customRange check, no preserve-existing-window logic), no historical fix, and it is not a misread of the code path. One sub-claim is inaccurate and should be discounted: 'or just touches it' — Radix Select does not fire onValueChange when the already-selected value is re-selected, so merely reopening/reselecting 'monthly' does NOT overwrite; the destructive path requires an actual value change (monthly→one-time→monthly, or any flip). Even the single one-time toggle (215-216) destroys the custom window. Severity is genuinely low: it requires deliberate Frequency-dropdown toggling on an expense that already carries a custom sub-period, and the changed dates are visible in the (auto-opened) Custom date range inputs — but it is silent (no warning) and produces wrong money on save, meeting the finding bar. Minimal leak: lines 219-220 (monthly branch widens to full lease) and symmetrically 215-216 (one-time branch collapses to a single day) — neither preserves the expense's existing window. A correct fix derives restore bounds from the expense's prior persisted dates, or leaves the date fields untouched on frequency-flip.

broken.title: Org-settings PATCH permanently 422-locks any realm whose currency is one of the 153 valid ISO currencies the UI offers but the server rejects (form offers 167, server whitelists 14)
broken.line: realmmanager.ts:227-229 (validateEnum currency); LandlordForm.js:63-79 (cc.data → 167 options), LandlordForm.js:33 (client zod z.string().min(1)), LandlordForm.js:189 (onSubmit re-sends currency every PATCH), LandlordForm.js:122 (initialValues.currency = existing); validators.ts:51-66 (CURRENCIES=14)

Client zod is only z.string().min(1) — no whitelist. update() calls validateEnum(req.body.currency, CURRENCIES, 'currency') unconditionally when currency !== undefined, and CURRENCIES has only [EUR,USD,GBP,BRL,COP,AUD,CAD,CHF,JPY,CNY,INR,NOK,SEK,DKK]=14. onSubmit's update branch ALWAYS includes currency: landlord.currency (line 189), which is initialValues.currency = the existing org currency (line 122). So once a realm carries any of the other 153 currencies (MXN, PLN, ZAR, AED, BGN...), every settings PATCH — even one that only renames the org or edits companyInfo — fails server-side validateEnum with HTTP 422 'Invalid currency'. The user cannot save ANY organization setting again.
broken.trigger: Pick e.g. Mexican Peso (MXN) in the org-settings currency dropdown (it is offered and is a valid ISO code Intl accepts: verified '100,00 MX$') → save once succeeds via add()? broken.moneyImpact: Not a wrong-money number, but a hard reject-valid-data lockout: a landlord operating in any of 153 legitimate currencies cannot edit organization settings (name, locale, company info, third-party emailer/SMS, bank info) because the form re-submits the rejected currency on every PATCH.

verdict.codeEvidence:
CURRENCIES whitelist = 14 codes (services/api/src/validators.ts:51-66): EUR,USD,GBP,BRL,COP,AUD,CAD,CHF,JPY,CNY,INR,NOK,SEK,DKK.

Form dropdown built from currency-codes filtered by getSymbolFromCurrency (LandlordForm.js:63-79): `...cc.data.reduce((acc,{code,currency})=>{ const symbol=getSymbolFromCurrency(code); if(symbol){acc.push(...)} ...})`. I executed this exact reduce in the landlord workspace: **offered=167, server=14, rejected-but-offered=153** including MXN, PLN, ZAR, AED, BGN, RUB, TRY, HKD, SGD, NZD, THB, HUF.

Client zod = no whitelist (LandlordForm.js:33): `currency: z.string().min(1)`. Dropdown renders all 167 (LandlordForm.js:277-283 `{currencies.filter((c) => c.value).map(...)}`).

add() persists currency unvalidated — realmmanager.ts:143-216 validates only name (line 161 validateStringField) and locale (lines 169-172 validateEnum). There is NO validateEnum(currency,...) in add(), so a non-whitelisted-but-offered code is saved at creation.

update() rejects it on EVERY PATCH when present (realmmanager.ts:227-229):
```
if (req.body.currency !== undefined) {
  validateEnum(req.body.currency, CURRENCIES, 'currency');
}
```
validateEnum throws 422 for non-members (validators.ts:155-160): `if (!allowed.includes(value as T)) { throw new ServiceError(\`Invalid ${fieldName}: '${value}'...\`, 422); }`.

onSubmit always re-sends currency (LandlordForm.js:186-191): `const updatedOrgPart = { name, isCompany, currency: landlord.currency, locale };` where landlord.currency defaults to initialValues.currency = organization?.currency (line 122) when the user only edits another field.

mergeOrganization spreads orgPart last so currency is always in the PATCH body, never undefined (utils.js:47-58): `const mergedOrg = { ...organization, thirdParties: {...}, ...orgPart };`.

Route: realmsRouter.patch('/:id', ...realmManager.update) (routes.ts:146-148) — no other currency-sanitizing middleware.
verdict.reasoning: I independently opened all three files and traced every link against disk. The whitelist/offered asymmetry is exact (153 valid ISO codes offered by the dropdown are rejected by the server — confirmed by running the dropdown's own reduce). The lockout is fully wired: (1) add() has no currency validation, so a code like MXN persists at creation; (2) update() runs validateEnum(currency, CURRENCIES) whenever currency is present and throws 422 for any of the 153; (3) onSubmit always populates updatedOrgPart.currency from landlord.currency, which defaults to the existing org currency when untouched; (4) mergeOrganization spreads orgPart last, so the rejected currency is in every PATCH body. Therefore any realm carrying one of the 153 codes can never save ANY organization setting (name, locale, companyInfo, third-party emailer/SMS/bank config) through the UI — a hard reject-valid-data lockout. The reviewer's only minor imprecisions are cosmetic: validateEnum's locale call at line 221 runs unconditionally (not the currency gate), but locale always passes because the dropdown only offers valid locales, so it doesn't change the outcome; and the dropdown is the only currency input, so the trigger is reachable. The finding HOLDS as BROKEN. Minimal leak: the form's 167-option dropdown (LandlordForm.js:63-79) vs the server's 14-code CURRENCIES (validators.ts:51-66), combined with currency being re-sent on every PATCH (LandlordForm.js:189). Minimal fix would be to align the dropdown to CURRENCIES (or broaden CURRENCIES to the full ISO set Intl accepts), and/or guard update() to skip re-validating an unchanged currency.

verdict.codeEvidence:
HEAD confirmed: `git rev-parse HEAD` → f6f759662e453d0d1a7f4f47cf421e28a98209c0, branch nas.

add() — services/api/src/managers/realmmanager.ts:143-216. The only field-level guards on the POST body are:
  L160-165: `req.body.name = validateStringField(req.body.name, 'name', { min:1, max:200, required:true });`

There is NO `validateEnum(..., CURRENCIES, 'currency')` anywhere in add(). The body is then handed straight to Mongoose at L174: `const newRealm: any = new Collections.Realm(req.body);` and persisted at L215: `res.json(_escapeSecrets(await newRealm.save()));`.

_hasRequiredFields — realmmanager.ts:51: `{ name: 'currency', provided: !!realm.currency },` — truthiness ONLY; any non-empty string passes (L54-58 throws 422 only when falsy).

update() DOES validate — realmmanager.ts:227-229:
  `if (req.body.currency !== undefined) {`
  `  validateEnum(req.body.currency, CURRENCIES, 'currency');`
  `}`
(comment L223-226 cites "Wave-21 C29-B1 ... Intl.NumberFormat ... RangeError ... 500"). This guard is NOT mirrored onto add().

grep for `currency` in realmmanager.ts returns only L51, L223, L227, L228 — confirming the sole ISO-validation call (L228) lives in update().

Schema — services/common/src/collections/realm.ts:114: `currency: String` (no enum, no validate fn).

CURRENCIES whitelist — services/api/src/validators.ts:51-66: ['EUR','USD','GBP','BRL','COP','AUD','CAD','CHF','JPY','CNY','INR','NOK','SEK','DKK'] (14 codes). validateEnum at validators.ts:143-162 throws ServiceError 422 for values not in the list.

Route wiring — services/api/src/routes.ts:145: `realmsRouter.post('/', Middlewares.asyncWrapper(realmManager.add as any));` → mounted at `/realms` (routes.ts:154).
verdict.reasoning:
The claim HOLDS as BROKEN. I traced the exact path: POST /realms → realmManager.add (routes.ts:145) → add() (realmmanager.ts:143). Inside add(), only `name` (validateStringField L160-165) and `locale` (validateEnum L169-172) are validated. Currency is never run through validateEnum(CURRENCIES). The only currency check reachable from add() is _hasRequiredFields L51, which is a pure truthiness test (`!!realm.currency`) — `currency:'NOTACURRENCY'` is truthy and passes. The Mongoose schema field (realm.ts:114) is a bare `currency: String` with no enum, so `new Collections.Realm(req.body)` + `.save()` persists the arbitrary string verbatim. The identical guard that closes this hole exists in update() (L227-229, "Wave-21 C29-B1") but was never mirrored onto add(). So a POST /realms with `currency:'NOTACURRENCY'` (or any of the ~139 ISO codes not in the 14-entry whitelist, e.g. MXN) returns 200 and persists a non-validated currency. This matches the reviewer's TITLE, FILE, and all cited line numbers exactly (verified against disk).

The reviewer's downstream IMPACT chain ("feeds the 422-lockout" and "crashes accounting via Intl.NumberFormat RangeError") is plausible and consistent with the in-code comment at update() L223-226, but I did not independently re-trace the accounting CSV crash here — that is a separate finding. For THIS finding (add() lacks the currency-whitelist guard that update() enforces, so an arbitrary currency string persists), the defect is real in current code. Minimal leak location: realmmanager.ts add(), between L172 and L174 — a mirror of `if (req.body.currency !== undefined) validateEnum(req.body.currency, CURRENCIES, 'currency');` is missing. Severity medium is reasonable: it accepts invalid data (a config-integrity defect) and is the precondition for currency-formatting failures on accounting surfaces.

broken.title: Accounting JSON endpoint and all 3 CSV exports throw an uncaught Intl RangeError/TypeError 500 when realm.currency is an invalid/non-ISO string — _settlements builds the formatter unconditionally even on the rawData JSON path
broken.line: _settlements NumberFormat constructed unconditionally at accountingmanager.ts:282-286 (NOT gated on !rawData, unlike _incomingTenants:169-175 and _outgoingTenants:217-223); reached by JSON all() at accountingmanager.ts:410 (rawData defaults true) and by settlementsAsCsv:479
broken.brokenShape: _incomingTenants/_outgoingTenants build Intl.NumberFormat only when !rawData. _settlements builds it ALWAYS (line 282: const NumberFormat = Intl.NumberFormat(locale, {style:'currency', currency, minimumFractionDigits:2})), so even the on-screen Accounting page (GET /accounting/:year → all() → _settlements with rawData=true) constructs the formatter with realm.currency. Verified: Intl.NumberFormat('el',{style:'currency',currency:'NOTACUR'}) → RangeError 'Invalid currency code'; currency:undefined → TypeError 'Currency code is required'; currency:'' → RangeError. With add() not validating currency (prior finding), a non-ISO currency reaches here and throws an uncaught error → HTTP 500 on the entire Accounting page load, not just the CSV download.
broken.trigger: Create a realm via direct POST /realms with currency:'NOTACURRENCY' (add() accepts it), add one tenant with a rent in the year, open the Accounting page (GET /api/v2/accounting/2026) → _settlements line 282 throws RangeError → 500. Same for GET .../accounting/2026/csv/settlements.
broken.moneyImpact: Entire accounting reconciliation surface (settlements grid + all 3 CSV exports) becomes unreachable — the landlord cannot view or export year-end payment settlements at all.

verdict.reasoning:
The claim holds on every link of the chain, verified against disk at HEAD f6f75966.

1) Structural asymmetry is real: _settlements (line 282) builds Intl.NumberFormat unconditionally; the two sibling builders gate construction on !rawData and substitute an identity {format: v=>v} on the rawData path. So even the on-screen Accounting JSON (all() → _settlements with default rawData=true, line 410) constructs the formatter with realm.currency — the reviewer's heightened-severity point (the whole Accounting page, not just CSV) is correct.

2) The load-bearing premise — that an invalid currency can reach here — is also real. add() (the realm-creation path, POST /realms per routes.ts:145) validates name and locale but NOT currency; the currency validateEnum guard lives only in update(). The Realm schema's currency is a bare String (no enum/default), and _hasRequiredFields only checks truthiness, so 'NOTACUR' persists via direct POST /realms.

3) The throw is real: I empirically confirmed Intl.NumberFormat with 'NOTACUR'/undefined/'' all throw (RangeError/TypeError/RangeError), matching the reviewer's prediction.

4) The 500 mapping is real: asyncWrapper does .catch(next); the errorHandler defaults to status 500 for any error that is not a ServiceError, MulterError, numeric-status error, or Mongo dup-key. A bare RangeError from Intl is none of those.

Therefore POST /realms {currency:'NOTACUR'} + one tenant with a rent in the year, then GET /api/v2/accounting/2026 (or .../csv/settlements), throws an uncaught RangeError at accountingmanager.ts:282 → HTTP 500. The entire settlements grid (JSON) and all three CSV exports become unreachable. This is not round-1 territory (round 1 covered the rent pipeline/building allocation/dashboard, not the realm-money-config → accounting Intl formatter path) and is not yet guarded — the update()-only currency validation explicitly anticipated this exact failure mode but was never extended to add() or to the rawData branch of _settlements.

Minimal leak / fix location: accountingmanager.ts:282 — gate the formatter like its siblings (`const NumberFormat = !rawData ? Intl.NumberFormat(...) : { format: (v)=>v };`). A defense-in-depth complement is adding `if (req.body.currency !== undefined) validateEnum(req.body.currency, CURRENCIES, 'currency');` to add() at realmmanager.ts ~line 172. Severity medium as stated: it bricks the year-end reconciliation surface but requires a non-ISO currency to have been saved (only reachable via the unvalidated add() path or a legacy/direct-DB row).

broken.title: Zero-decimal currencies (JPY) render with two forced decimal places on every money surface — the forced minimumFractionDigits:2 overrides the ISO-4217 zero-fraction rule
broken.line: accountingmanager.ts:172/174, 219/221, 283/285 (minimumFractionDigits:2); pdfgenerator templatefunctions.ts:24-28 (minimumFractionDigits=2 default); numberformat.js:5-11 (minimumFractionDigits=2 default); JPY is whitelisted at validators.ts:60
broken.brokenShape: JPY is an accepted currency (CURRENCIES includes 'JPY', validators.ts:60). Every currency formatter in the codebase forces minimumFractionDigits:2. Verified: Intl.NumberFormat('en',{style:'currency',currency:'JPY'}).format(1234.5) = '¥1,235' (correct, 0 decimals), but with minimumFractionDigits:2 = '¥1,234.50' (wrong — yen has no sub-unit). This is identical across the accounting CSV/JSON, the PDF receipt/owner-statement/rent-call, and the frontend useFormatNumber, so the wrong-decimal rendering is consistent but consistently wrong for a zero-decimal currency.
broken.trigger: A realm with currency:'JPY' (offered in the dropdown, whitelisted server-side). Any rent receipt PDF, accounting export, or on-screen amount renders e.g. ¥1,234.50 instead of ¥1,235.
broken.moneyImpact: Wrong-locale money rendering for zero-decimal currencies (JPY and any future addition like KRW). Cosmetic-but-incorrect on bills/receipts; does not drop or double-count money.

verdict.codeEvidence:
CURRENT code at HEAD f6f75966 (verified `git rev-parse HEAD` = f6f759662e...), branch nas.

1) validators.ts:51-66 whitelists JPY (and CNY) as accepted realm currencies:
```
51  const CURRENCIES = [
52    'EUR',
...
60    'JPY',
61    'CNY',
...
66  ] as const;
```

2) Frontend offers JPY in the dropdown — LandlordForm.js:63-79 builds the currency list from the full `currency-codes` library, filtered only by symbol availability (JPY → ¥):
```
65    ...cc.data
66      .reduce((acc, { code, currency }) => {
67        const symbol = getSymbolFromCurrency(code);
68        if (symbol) { acc.push({ code, currency, symbol }); }
```

3) Every money formatter forces minimumFractionDigits:2:
- accountingmanager.ts _incomingTenants:170-174, _outgoingTenants:218-222, _settlements:282-286 — all `Intl.NumberFormat(locale,{style:'currency',currency,minimumFractionDigits:2})`.
- pdfgenerator templatefunctions.ts:22-28 — `formatNumber(value, style='decimal', minimumFractionDigits=2)`; for style 'currency' passes `minimumFractionDigits` (defaulted 2) into Intl.NumberFormat with realm currency. PDF templates invoke `_.formatNumber(rent.total.grandTotal,'currency')` with no 3rd arg (rentcall.ejs:22, rentcalltotal.ejs:4/10/16/21, invoicebody.ejs:51-52) → default 2.
- numberformat.js:1-12 — `formatNumber(locale='en',currency='EUR',value,minimumFractionDigits=2)`. useFormatNumber.js:10-17 passes through `minimumFractionDigits` which is `undefined` for the common `style==='currency'` call → re-defaults to 2.

4) Runtime confirmation that the forced floor overrides the ISO-4217 zero-fraction rule (Intl bumps maximumFractionDigits to match the min):
```
Intl.NumberFormat('en',{style:'currency',currency:'JPY',minimumFractionDigits:2}).format(1234.5)  => '¥1,234.50'   (resolvedOptions: max=2)
Intl.NumberFormat('en',{style:'currency',currency:'JPY'}).format(1234.5)                          => '¥1,235'      (resolvedOptions: max=0, correct)
Intl.NumberFormat('el',{style:'currency',currency:'JPY',minimumFractionDigits:2}).format(1234.5)  => '1.234,50 JP¥'
```
verdict.reasoning: I independently opened all three cited files at HEAD f6f75966 and confirmed every cited line matches disk: minimumFractionDigits:2 is hardcoded in accountingmanager.ts (173/221/285 — i.e. the second line of each NumberFormat block at 170-174, 218-222, 282-286), defaulted to 2 in templatefunctions.ts:22 and numberformat.js:5, and JPY is whitelisted at validators.ts:60. The critical technical question — does a forced minimumFractionDigits:2 actually override ISO-4217's zero-fraction rule? — I verified at runtime: yes. Intl.NumberFormat raises maximumFractionDigits to 2 to satisfy the minimum, yielding '¥1,234.50' instead of the correct '¥1,235'. The path is fully reachable: JPY is populated in the UI currency dropdown from cc.data (LandlordForm.js) and accepted by the server validator, and all PDF/CSV/frontend currency calls omit the per-currency fraction arg so they fall back to the hardcoded 2. The bug is real and consistent across the accounting CSV/JSON, every PDF (rent-call/reminder/invoice/receipt), and on-screen useFormatNumber. It is cosmetic — no money is dropped, double-counted, or mis-summed; the underlying numeric values are unchanged, only the rendered decimal places are wrong for zero-fraction currencies (JPY, and any future KRW/CLP/etc). This matches the reviewer's severity-low classification. No guard exists anywhere that special-cases zero-decimal currencies (no maximumFractionDigits override, no currency-fraction lookup table). The claim HOLDS as a real but low-severity rendering defect; minimal leak is the hardcoded `minimumFractionDigits: 2` / default `= 2` in the four formatter sites.
